```rust
// PURPOSE:
// End-to-end test: the real Rust bridge against a real Python server.
//
// Every other test in this workspace is one-sided. The bridge's own tests prove
// it encodes a request correctly; the Python suite proves the servicer reads
// one correctly. Neither proves the two implementations actually agree on the
// wire -- and a disagreement there is silent in production, because each side
// looks correct in isolation while the call simply fails.
//
// So this test spawns a real Python server and drives it with a real
// `GrpcAgentBridge` over a real TCP socket.
//
// It skips, rather than fails, when Python or the orchestrator package is not
// installed, so `cargo test` stays usable in a Rust-only environment. A skipped
// end-to-end test is visible in the run summary; a hard failure would not be.

//! Cross-language end-to-end test.
//!
//! Drives [`GrpcAgentBridge`] against a real Python orchestrator process.
//! Nothing is mocked on the wire: the request is really encoded by Rust, really
//! sent over TCP, really authorized and executed by Python, and the reply is
//! really decoded back into an [`AgentRunVerdict`].
//!
//! Set `MAS_E2E_STUB` to override the server script's location.

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
use std::process::{Child, Command, Stdio};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use mas_ai_bridge::{GrpcAgentBridge, GrpcAgentBridgeConfig};
use mas_common::enums::Environment;
use mas_common::ids::{AgentId, OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId};
use mas_domain::{ResourceLimits, TokenBudget};
use mas_execution::agent_bridge::{AgentBridge, AgentRunRequest, AgentRunVerdict};
use mas_orchestration::runtime_context::RuntimeContext;
use mas_security::secret_string::SecretString;
use uuid::Uuid;

/// Credential the Python stub accepts. Mirrors its `DEFAULT_TOKEN`.
const TOKEN: &str = "bridge-service-token";
/// Subject the Python stub expects. Mirrors its `DEFAULT_SUBJECT`.
const SUBJECT: &str = "rust-core";

/// The Python harness, resolved from the environment or by convention.
fn stub_script() -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
    if let Ok(path) = std::env::var("MAS_E2E_STUB") {
        return Some(std::path::PathBuf::from(path));
    }
    // This file lives at <workspace>/crates/ai-bridge/tests/. `..` walks back
    // to <workspace>, so five levels reach the checkout root that holds
    // `python-orchestrator/` beside the Rust tree. Probed rather than assumed:
    // a wrong guess here once made every test below report "passed" while
    // silently doing nothing.
    let root = std::path::PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../../../..");
    let relative = "python-orchestrator/tests/bridge/stub_server.py";
    [
        root.join(relative),
        std::path::PathBuf::from("/home/user").join(relative),
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .find(|base| base.is_file())
}

/// Whether the Python side is usable at all.
fn python_available(script: &std::path::Path) -> bool {
    Command::new("python3")
        .arg("-c")
        .arg("import mas_orchestrator")
        .stdout(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .status()
        .map(|status| status.success())
        .unwrap_or(false)
        && script.is_file()
}

/// A running Python server, terminated on drop.
///
/// Holding the child in a guard matters: if an assertion panics mid-test the
/// process still has to go, or a stray server keeps a port bound and makes
/// later runs fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the failure.
struct Server {
    child: Child,
    port: u16,
}

impl Drop for Server {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.child.kill();
        let _ = self.child.wait();
    }
}

/// Starts the Python server and returns once it reports its port.
fn spawn(behaviour: &str, delay: f64) -> Option<Server> {
    let script = stub_script()?;
    if !python_available(&script) {
        return None;
    }

    let mut child = Command::new("python3")
        .arg(&script)
        .arg("--behaviour")
        .arg(behaviour)
        .arg("--delay")
        .arg(delay.to_string())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .spawn()
        .ok()?;

    // The server prints its port once it is listening. Reading that line is
    // the readiness signal: connecting on a guess would race the bind.
    let stdout = child.stdout.take()?;
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(stdout);
    let mut line = String::new();
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);

    loop {
        line.clear();
        match reader.read_line(&mut line) {
            Ok(0) => break,
            Ok(_) => {
                if let Some(value) = line.trim().strip_prefix("PORT=") {
                    if let Ok(port) = value.parse::<u16>() {
                        return Some(Server { child, port });
                    }
                }
            },
            Err(_) => break,
        }
        if Instant::now() > deadline {
            break;
        }
    }

    let _ = child.kill();
    None
}

/// Builds a bridge pointed at `port`, with the credential the stub accepts.
fn bridge(port: u16) -> GrpcAgentBridgeConfig {
    GrpcAgentBridgeConfig {
        endpoint: format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"),
        default_timeout: Duration::from_secs(20),
        max_response_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
        bearer_token: Some(SecretString::new(TOKEN.to_owned())),
        service_subject: SUBJECT.to_owned(),
        service_issuer: "platform-mtls".to_owned(),
        service_scopes: vec!["execute_agent".to_owned()],
    }
}

/// Builds a properly scoped run request.
fn request() -> AgentRunRequest {
    let context = RuntimeContext::new(
        TenantId::new(),
        OrganizationId::new(),
        ProjectId::new(),
        "e2e",
        Environment::Development,
    )
    .expect("context");

    AgentRunRequest::from_context(
        &context,
        AgentId::new(),
        serde_json::json!({"prompt": "hello from rust"}),
        ResourceLimits::default(),
        &TokenBudget::unlimited(),
    )
    .expect("request")
}

/// Skips the test with a visible reason when the Python side is missing.
macro_rules! require_python {
    ($server:expr) => {{
        match $server {
            Some(server) => server,
            None => {
                eprintln!(
                    "SKIPPED: the Python orchestrator is not available; \
                     install it (`pip install -e .`) or set MAS_E2E_STUB"
                );
                return;
            },
        }
    }};
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_successful_run_crosses_the_language_boundary() {
    let server = require_python!(spawn("success", 0.0));
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(bridge(server.port))
        .await
        .expect("connect");

    let verdict = bridge.run(request()).await.expect("run");

    match verdict {
        AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { output, usage: _ } => {
            assert_eq!(
                output,
                serde_json::json!("the answer"),
                "output round-tripped"
            );
        },
        AgentRunVerdict::Failed { code, message, .. } => {
            panic!("expected success, got failure {code}: {message}");
        },
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_python_failure_arrives_with_its_machine_readable_code() {
    let server = require_python!(spawn("failure", 0.0));
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(bridge(server.port))
        .await
        .expect("connect");

    let verdict = bridge.run(request()).await.expect("run");

    match verdict {
        AgentRunVerdict::Failed {
            code,
            message,
            retryable,
            usage: _,
        } => {
            assert_eq!(
                code, "model_timeout",
                "the domain code must survive the hop"
            );
            assert!(retryable, "a provider timeout is transient");
            assert!(!message.is_empty(), "the failure carries a message");
        },
        AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { .. } => panic!("expected failure, got success"),
    }
}

/// Builds a run request under an explicitly chosen scope.
///
/// The default `request()` mints random ids, which is right for the tests above
/// but useless for isolation: to prove a run executed under *this* tenant, the
/// caller has to know which tenant it asked for.
fn scoped_request(tenant: Uuid, organization: Uuid, project: Uuid) -> AgentRunRequest {
    let context = RuntimeContext::new(
        TenantId::from(tenant),
        OrganizationId::from(organization),
        ProjectId::from(project),
        "e2e",
        Environment::Development,
    )
    .expect("context");

    AgentRunRequest::from_context(
        &context,
        AgentId::new(),
        serde_json::json!({"prompt": "hello from rust"}),
        ResourceLimits::default(),
        &TokenBudget::unlimited(),
    )
    .expect("request")
}

/// Reads the scope the Python side reported back.
fn reported_scope(output: &serde_json::Value) -> serde_json::Value {
    // The stub answers with a JSON document rather than prose, so the caller
    // can compare fields instead of substring-matching a sentence.
    serde_json::from_str(output.as_str().expect("a JSON string")).expect("scope document")
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn each_run_executes_under_the_scope_rust_sent() {
    // Tenant isolation is a property no single side can prove. Rust can assert
    // it puts a tenant on the wire; Python can assert it reads one. Neither can
    // show that the run actually executed under the tenant the caller asked
    // for -- and a mismatch is silent, because both sides behave correctly
    // while the work happens in the wrong tenancy.
    let server = require_python!(spawn("echo_scope", 0.0));
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(bridge(server.port))
        .await
        .expect("connect");

    let tenants = [Uuid::from_u128(1), Uuid::from_u128(2)];
    let organizations = [Uuid::from_u128(11), Uuid::from_u128(12)];
    let projects = [Uuid::from_u128(21), Uuid::from_u128(22)];

    let mut reported = Vec::new();
    for index in 0..2 {
        let verdict = bridge
            .run(scoped_request(
                tenants[index],
                organizations[index],
                projects[index],
            ))
            .await
            .expect("run");

        let output = match verdict {
            AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { output, usage: _ } => output,
            AgentRunVerdict::Failed { code, message, .. } => {
                panic!("expected success, got {code}: {message}")
            },
        };
        reported.push(reported_scope(&output));
    }

    for index in 0..2 {
        let scope = &reported[index];
        assert_eq!(
            scope["tenant_id"].as_str().expect("tenant_id"),
            tenants[index].to_string(),
            "run {index} executed under the caller's tenant"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            scope["organization_id"].as_str().expect("organization_id"),
            organizations[index].to_string(),
            "run {index} executed under the caller's organization"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            scope["project_id"].as_str().expect("project_id"),
            projects[index].to_string(),
            "run {index} executed under the caller's project"
        );
    }

    // The decisive assertion: two runs on one connection must not share scope.
    // A server that cached or leaked context between calls would answer one of
    // these with the other's tenant, and every per-field check above would
    // still have passed for whichever call came first.
    assert_ne!(
        reported[0]["tenant_id"], reported[1]["tenant_id"],
        "concurrent runs on one connection must not share a tenant"
    );
    assert_ne!(
        reported[0]["organization_id"], reported[1]["organization_id"],
        "concurrent runs on one connection must not share an organization"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_failure_never_carries_a_credential_across_the_wire() {
    // The stub raises an error whose own text embeds an API-key-shaped value
    // and a bearer token. That is not contrived: a provider adapter raises
    // while a credential is in scope, so the key can end up inside the error's
    // own message.
    //
    // This is the one property here that cannot be checked by reading either
    // side alone. Python can prove it redacts; Rust can prove it does not log
    // what it receives. Only crossing the boundary shows whether the redacted
    // text is what actually arrives -- and a leak is silent, because nothing
    // fails, the secret simply travels.
    let server = require_python!(spawn("leak", 0.0));
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(bridge(server.port))
        .await
        .expect("connect");

    let message = match bridge.run(request()).await.expect("run") {
        AgentRunVerdict::Failed { message, .. } => message,
        AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { .. } => panic!("the leak stub must fail"),
    };

    const LEAKED_KEY: &str = "sk-AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA";
    const LEAKED_BEARER: &str = "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.ZmFrZS1wYXlsb2Fk.c2lnbmF0dXJl";

    assert!(
        !message.contains(LEAKED_KEY),
        "an API key reached the caller: {message}"
    );
    assert!(
        !message.contains(LEAKED_BEARER),
        "a bearer token reached the caller: {message}"
    );
    // The call's own credential must not be echoed back either.
    assert!(
        !message.contains(TOKEN),
        "the caller's own credential was echoed back: {message}"
    );
    assert!(
        !message.is_empty(),
        "redaction must not silence the failure entirely"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_wrong_credential_is_refused() {
    let server = require_python!(spawn("success", 0.0));
    let mut config = bridge(server.port);
    config.bearer_token = Some(SecretString::new("not-the-token".to_owned()));
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(config).await.expect("connect");

    let error = bridge
        .run(request())
        .await
        .expect_err("a forged credential must not be honoured");

    // The important property is that this is an *authorization* failure and
    // not a success. It must also not be retryable: replaying a rejected
    // credential just burns the caller's retry budget.
    //
    // And it must not be an ExternalService error. That variant is what a
    // transport failure maps to, and it is retryable -- so asserting only on
    // retryability would let "the server was unreachable" pass as "the server
    // rejected us". The test has to tell those apart or it proves nothing.
    assert!(
        !matches!(error, mas_common::AppError::ExternalService { .. }),
        "a rejection must not be reported as a transport failure: {error}"
    );
    assert!(
        !error.is_retryable(),
        "a rejected credential is terminal: {error}"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_missing_credential_is_refused() {
    let server = require_python!(spawn("success", 0.0));
    let mut config = bridge(server.port);
    config.bearer_token = None;
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(config).await.expect("connect");

    let error = bridge
        .run(request())
        .await
        .expect_err("an unauthenticated call must not be honoured");

    assert!(
        !matches!(error, mas_common::AppError::ExternalService { .. }),
        "a rejection must not be reported as a transport failure: {error}"
    );
    assert!(
        !error.is_retryable(),
        "a missing credential is not transient: {error}"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_subject_that_disagrees_with_the_credential_is_refused() {
    // The token authenticates the subject "rust-core". Declaring a different
    // subject in the body is exactly the forgery the orchestrator exists to
    // catch: the body is attacker-influenced in a way the bearer credential is
    // not, so the two must be reconciled rather than the body believed.
    let server = require_python!(spawn("success", 0.0));
    let mut config = bridge(server.port);
    config.service_subject = "someone-else".to_owned();
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(config).await.expect("connect");

    let error = bridge
        .run(request())
        .await
        .expect_err("a declared subject must not override the authenticated one");

    assert!(
        !matches!(error, mas_common::AppError::ExternalService { .. }),
        "a rejection must not be reported as a transport failure: {error}"
    );
    assert!(
        !error.is_retryable(),
        "a rejected identity is terminal: {error}"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_deadline_the_python_side_cannot_meet_is_not_a_success() {
    // A slow server plus a tight Rust deadline. The run may fail with a timeout
    // or be cancelled; what it must never do is return Succeeded, because the
    // platform would then build on output from a run that was cut short.
    let server = require_python!(spawn("success", 5.0));
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(bridge(server.port))
        .await
        .expect("connect");

    let mut request = request();
    request.deadline =
        mas_orchestration::timeout::Deadline::after(Duration::from_millis(400)).expires_at();

    match bridge.run(request).await {
        Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { .. }) => {
            panic!("a run stopped by its deadline must not be reported as success")
        },
        Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Failed { code, .. }) => {
            assert!(
                !code.is_empty(),
                "the failure carries a machine-readable code"
            );
        },
        Err(error) => assert!(
            matches!(error, mas_common::AppError::Timeout(_))
                || matches!(error, mas_common::AppError::Cancelled(_)),
            "expected a timeout or cancellation, got {error:?}"
        ),
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_cancelled_run_is_never_reported_as_success() {
    let server = require_python!(spawn("hang", 0.0));
    let bridge = GrpcAgentBridge::connect(bridge(server.port))
        .await
        .expect("connect");

    let mut request = request();
    request.cancellation.cancel();
    request.deadline =
        mas_orchestration::timeout::Deadline::after(Duration::from_millis(500)).expires_at();

    // Whether the run is stopped by the deadline or by the cancellation, the
    // one unacceptable answer is "Succeeded". A platform that records a
    // cancelled run as completed will build on output that does not exist.
    let outcome = bridge.run(request).await;

    match outcome {
        Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { .. }) => {
            panic!("a cancelled run must never be reported as success")
        },
        Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Failed { code, .. }) => {
            assert_eq!(
                code, "cancellation_requested",
                "cancellations carry one code"
            );
        },
        Err(error) => assert!(
            matches!(error, mas_common::AppError::Cancelled(_))
                || matches!(error, mas_common::AppError::Timeout(_)),
            "expected a cancellation or timeout, got {error:?}"
        ),
    }
}
```

```proto
// PURPOSE:
// The canonical wire contract between Rust and Python.
//
// Declares `AgentBridgeApi`, the only surface Rust uses to ask Python to run
// an agent, together with every message that crosses it: the request carrying
// request/execution/task/tenant/org/project identity, the authenticated
// service identity, a correlation id, an absolute deadline, an idempotency
// key, the agent reference and version, the input, runtime state and tool
// context; and the reply carrying the result, a structured failure with a
// machine-readable code, safe provider metadata, usage, cost, the finish
// state, correlation/request identity and retry classification.
//
// Both languages generate from THIS file. Editing it is a breaking change on
// both sides, and it is the only place the contract is defined.

// Multi-Agent System public gRPC API (v1).
//
// Semantics are IDENTICAL to the HTTP surface: the same use-cases, the same
// validation errors, the same idempotency rules, the same existence hiding.
// Scope travels as metadata: `x-tenant-id` + `x-organization-id` (uuid
// strings); identity as `authorization: Bearer …`; correlation as
// `x-correlation-id` (generated server-side when absent); execution
// idempotency via `idempotency-key`.
syntax = "proto3";
package mas.api.v1;

// ------------------------------ shared ------------------------------------
message Empty {}

message ExecutionReply {
  string execution_id = 1;
  string status = 2;
  string tenant_id = 3;
  optional string workflow_id = 4;
  optional string agent_id = 5;
  string root_execution_id = 6;
  string correlation_id = 7;
  bool cancellation_requested = 8;
  bool replayed = 9;
  string failure = 10;  // empty when no failure
  string output_json = 11;  // empty when incomplete
}

// ------------------------------ tenancy ------------------------------------
service TenancyApi {
  rpc RegisterOrganization(RegisterOrganizationRequest) returns (OrganizationReply);
  rpc ListOrganizations(Empty) returns (ListOrganizationsReply);
  rpc RegisterTenant(RegisterTenantRequest) returns (TenantReply);
  rpc ListTenants(Empty) returns (ListTenantsReply);
  rpc RegisterProject(RegisterProjectRequest) returns (ProjectReply);
  rpc InviteMembership(InviteMembershipRequest) returns (MembershipReply);
}

message RegisterOrganizationRequest {
  string legal_name = 1;
  string display_name = 2;
  string slug = 3;
}
message OrganizationReply { string id = 1; string legal_name = 2; string display_name = 3; string slug = 4; }
message ListOrganizationsReply { repeated OrganizationReply organizations = 1; }

message RegisterTenantRequest {
  string name = 1;
  string slug = 2;
  string environment = 3;  // development|staging|production
  string isolation = 4;    // shared_rls|schema_per_tenant|dedicated_database
}
message TenantReply { string id = 1; string name = 2; string slug = 3; string environment = 4; string isolation = 5; }
message ListTenantsReply { repeated TenantReply tenants = 1; }

message RegisterProjectRequest { string name = 1; string slug = 2; }
message ProjectReply { string id = 1; string name = 2; string slug = 3; }

message InviteMembershipRequest { string user_id = 1; string role = 2; }
message MembershipReply { string id = 1; string user_id = 2; string role = 3; string status = 4; }

// ------------------------------ agents --------------------------------------
service AgentApi {
  rpc RegisterAgent(RegisterAgentRequest) returns (AgentReply);
  rpc PublishAgentVersion(PublishAgentVersionRequest) returns (AgentVersionReply);
  rpc GetAgent(GetAgentRequest) returns (AgentReply);
  rpc ListAgents(ListAgentsRequest) returns (ListAgentsReply);
}

message RegisterAgentRequest {
  string project_id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  string slug = 3;
  string kind = 4;  // standard|supervisor|tool_user
}
message AgentReply {
  string id = 1;
  string project_id = 2;
  string tenant_id = 3;
  string name = 4;
  string slug = 5;
  string kind = 6;
  string status = 7;
  uint64 current_version = 8;  // 0 = none
}
message GetAgentRequest { string agent_id = 1; }
message ListAgentsRequest { string project_id = 1; }
message ListAgentsReply { repeated AgentReply agents = 1; }

message PublishAgentVersionRequest {
  string agent_id = 1;
  string configuration_checksum = 2;  // 64 lowercase hex chars
  string configuration_snapshot_json = 3;
  string published_by = 4;  // user uuid
}
message AgentVersionReply { string id = 1; uint64 version_number = 2; string checksum = 3; }

// ------------------------------ workflows ------------------------------------
service WorkflowApi {
  rpc CreateWorkflow(CreateWorkflowRequest) returns (WorkflowReply);
  rpc UpdateWorkflowGraph(UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest) returns (UpdateWorkflowGraphReply);
  rpc GetWorkflow(GetWorkflowRequest) returns (WorkflowReply);
  rpc ListWorkflows(ListWorkflowsRequest) returns (ListWorkflowsReply);
}

message CreateWorkflowRequest { string project_id = 1; string name = 2; }
message WorkflowReply { string id = 1; string project_id = 2; string name = 3; uint32 node_count = 4; uint64 graph_version = 5; }

message WorkflowNodeMsg {
  string node_key = 1;
  string node_type = 2;
  string name = 3;
  string config_json = 4;  // serialized JSON object
}
message WorkflowEdgeMsg { string from_key = 1; string to_key = 2; }
message UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest {
  string workflow_id = 1;
  repeated WorkflowNodeMsg nodes = 2;
  repeated WorkflowEdgeMsg edges = 3;
}
message UpdateWorkflowGraphReply { string workflow_id = 1; repeated string topological_order = 2; }
message GetWorkflowRequest { string workflow_id = 1; }
message ListWorkflowsRequest { string project_id = 1; }
message ListWorkflowsReply { repeated WorkflowReply workflows = 1; }

// ------------------------------ executions -----------------------------------
service ExecutionApi {
  rpc SubmitExecution(SubmitExecutionRequest) returns (ExecutionReply);
  rpc TransitionExecution(TransitionExecutionRequest) returns (ExecutionReply);
  rpc GetExecution(GetExecutionRequest) returns (ExecutionReply);
  rpc ListExecutions(Empty) returns (ListExecutionsReply);
}

message SubmitExecutionRequest {
  string project_id = 1;
  optional string workflow_id = 2;
  optional string agent_id = 3;
  string input_json = 4;
  // `idempotency-key` metadata header is authoritative.
}
message TransitionExecutionRequest {
  string execution_id = 1;
  TransitionAction action = 2;
}
enum TransitionAction {
  TRANSITION_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_START = 1;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_PAUSE = 2;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_RESUME = 3;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_CANCEL = 4;
}
message GetExecutionRequest { string execution_id = 1; }
message ListExecutionsReply { repeated ExecutionReply executions = 1; }

// ------------------------------ schedules ------------------------------------
service ScheduleApi {
  rpc RegisterSchedule(RegisterScheduleRequest) returns (ScheduleReply);
  rpc SetScheduleState(SetScheduleStateRequest) returns (ScheduleReply);
  rpc ListSchedules(Empty) returns (ListSchedulesReply);
}

message RegisterScheduleRequest {
  optional string project_id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  string kind = 3;  // "interval" (only uniform-choice exposed)
  uint64 every_seconds = 4;
  string task_template_json = 5;
}
enum ScheduleStateAction {
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_PAUSE = 1;
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_RESUME = 2;
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_DISABLE = 3;
}
message SetScheduleStateRequest { string schedule_id = 1; ScheduleStateAction action = 2; }
message ScheduleReply { string id = 1; string name = 2; string status = 3; }
message ListSchedulesReply { repeated ScheduleReply schedules = 1; }

// --------------------- AI orchestrator bridge -------------------------------
//
// Rust -> Python AI Orchestrator. Rust remains the caller and the sole
// authority on execution state; the orchestrator may not transition execution
// state on its own and may not write Rust-owned tables.
//
// This service exists because the Python orchestrator owns AI execution
// (agent behaviour, planning, model providers, tools, memory, RAG,
// guardrails), while Rust owns platform execution state. The messages below
// are a 1:1 projection of the Rust domain types:
//
//   AgentRunRequest   <- mas_execution::agent_bridge::AgentRunRequest
//   ResourceLimitsMsg <- mas_domain::ResourceLimits
//   AgentRunReply     <- mas_execution::agent_bridge::AgentRunVerdict
//   AgentUsageMsg     <- mas_execution::agent_bridge::AgentUsage
//
// Timestamps are RFC-3339 strings with millisecond precision
// (`Timestamp::to_rfc3339_millis`), matching the Rust serde representation so
// no lossy conversion is introduced at the boundary.
service AgentBridgeApi {
  // Runs an agent once. Retries belong to the caller's policy.
  rpc RunAgent(AgentRunRequest) returns (AgentRunReply);
  // Readiness of the AI runtime behind the bridge.
  rpc Health(Empty) returns (BridgeHealthReply);
}

// Resource envelope the AI runtime must respect (mirrors `ResourceLimits`).
message ResourceLimitsMsg {
  // Wall-clock timeout for the whole run, milliseconds.
  uint64 timeout_ms = 1;
  // Maximum number of execution steps.
  uint32 max_steps = 2;
  // Maximum concurrently running tasks spawned by this run.
  uint32 max_parallel_tasks = 3;
  // Maximum tool invocations.
  uint32 max_tool_calls = 4;
  // Maximum input/output payload size in bytes.
  uint64 max_payload_bytes = 5;
  // Maximum retries of any single step.
  uint32 max_retries = 6;
}

message AgentRunRequest {
  // ---- AI routing ---------------------------------------------------------
  string agent_id = 1;
  // Pinned agent version; empty means "current published version".
  optional string agent_version = 2;
  // JSON-encoded run input (already redacted upstream by Rust).
  string input_json = 3;

  // ---- identity / correlation (authoritative, supplied by Rust) ----------
  string correlation_id = 4;
  string request_id = 5;
  string execution_id = 6;
  string task_id = 7;
  string tenant_id = 8;
  string organization_id = 9;
  optional string project_id = 10;
  // Wire protocol version claimed by the caller; mismatched majors are
  // rejected before any AI work is performed.
  string protocol_version = 11;

  // ---- bounds -------------------------------------------------------------
  // Absolute wall-clock deadline, RFC-3339 with milliseconds.
  string deadline_rfc3339 = 12;
  ResourceLimitsMsg limits = 13;
  // Token allowance forwarded to the runtime (0 = unmetered).
  uint64 token_budget_max = 14;

  // ---- idempotency --------------------------------------------------------
  // Caller-supplied deduplication key. Rust derives it from the task's own
  // idempotency key, so a redelivered task cannot re-run paid AI work. Empty
  // means "no deduplication requested" and is legal for one-shot runs.
  optional string idempotency_key = 15;

  // ---- authenticated caller identity --------------------------------------
  // The authenticated internal service identity Rust resolved before making
  // this call. It travels in the *body* rather than only in metadata so the
  // orchestrator can authorize against a value Rust signed off on; the
  // `authorization` bearer header carries the same principal as proof of
  // possession and is cross-checked against this field.
  ServiceIdentityMsg identity = 16;
}

// Authenticated internal service identity (mirrors
// `mas_security::principal::ServicePrincipal`). Never contains a credential:
// the secret stays in the `authorization` header and is redacted everywhere.
message ServiceIdentityMsg {
  // Stable subject name, e.g. "rust-core".
  string subject = 1;
  // Issuer that vouched for the subject, e.g. "platform-mtls".
  string issuer = 2;
  // Scopes the subject holds, e.g. "execute_agent".
  repeated string scopes = 3;
}

// Agent self-reported consumption. Mirrors `AgentUsage`.
message AgentUsageMsg {
  uint64 tokens_input = 1;
  uint64 tokens_output = 2;
  uint32 tool_calls = 3;
  uint32 steps = 4;
  // Wall-clock active time reported by the agent, milliseconds.
  uint64 active_time_ms = 5;
}

message AgentSucceeded {
  // JSON-encoded output.
  string output_json = 1;
  AgentUsageMsg usage = 2;
  // Which model actually served the run, after routing and failover, as
  // "provider/model". Safe to log: it names a configured endpoint, never a
  // credential. Absent when the runtime did not record it.
  optional string model_key = 3;
  // Why the run stopped: "completed", "step_limit", "tool_call_limit",
  // "deadline", "cancelled", "budget_exhausted". Distinct from success: a run
  // can stop early with usable output.
  string finish_reason = 4;
}

message AgentFailed {
  // Stable machine-readable failure code (e.g. "model_timeout").
  string code = 1;
  // Safe message; never contains credentials or raw provider errors.
  string message = 2;
  // Whether the caller's retry policy may retry this run.
  bool retryable = 3;
  AgentUsageMsg usage = 4;
  // Correlation id of the work that failed, so a Rust log line can be joined
  // to the AI failure without a second lookup.
  string correlation_id = 5;
  // Platform request id of the call that failed.
  string request_id = 6;
}

message AgentRunReply {
  oneof verdict {
    AgentSucceeded succeeded = 1;
    AgentFailed failed = 2;
  }
}

message BridgeHealthReply {
  bool healthy = 1;
  // Human-readable detail; must never contain secret material.
  string detail = 2;
}
```

### FILE: `enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/api/src/main.rs`

**PURPOSE:**

_PURPOSE ব্লক এই ফাইলের হেডারে নেই; ফাইলটি জেনারেটেড বা কনফিগারেশন-মাত্র._

```rust
//! PURPOSE: `mas-api` process bootstrap: HTTP + gRPC servers over the
//! application layer with graceful shutdown.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge).
//!
//! Production responsibility: compose the real object graph once, bind the
//! listeners, install health/readiness probes, and shut down without dropping
//! in-flight requests. The `--dev-inmemory` lane exists for local bring-up and
//! is unreachable unless the flag is passed explicitly — production must never
//! start stateless by accident.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • contain request handling, business rules or SQL;
//!   • construct stores directly — composition comes from `state.rs`;
//!   • treat a missing production dependency as "start with a fallback".

//! `mas-api` process bootstrap: HTTP + gRPC servers over the application
//! layer with graceful shutdown.
//!
//! Two bring-up modes:
//! * `--dev-inmemory` — everything over `InMemoryServices` (local bring-up,
//!   NO persistence). Requires explicit flag so production never starts up
//!   stateless by accident.
//! * (default) — full production composition: PostgreSQL-backed stores via
//!   `mas_persistence::PgServices`, `engine` audit on `PostgresAuditLog`,
//!   bearer auth via `PostgresApiKeyVerifier`, migration verification at
//!   boot (deterministic fail-fast on drift; `MAS_DATABASE_MIGRATE_ON_BOOT`
//!   enables the deliberate apply path), and the DB dependency probe on the
//!   readiness surface.
//!
//! Environment:
//! * `MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR` (default `0.0.0.0:8080`)
//! * `MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR` (default `0.0.0.0:50051`)
//! * `MAS_DEV_TOKENS` (`token:subject:kind,...`; only with `--dev-inmemory`)

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::Arc;

use mas_api::auth::{PrincipalKind, StaticTokenVerifier};
use mas_api::server::ServerConfig;
use mas_api::state::AppState;
use mas_application::agent_service::AgentService;
use mas_application::audit::InMemoryAuditSink;
use mas_application::execution_service::ExecutionService;
use mas_application::schedule_service::ScheduleService;
use mas_application::stores::InMemoryServices;
use mas_application::tenancy_service::TenancyService;
use mas_application::workflow_service::WorkflowService;
use mas_observability::health::HealthRegistry;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    std::process::exit(match run().await {
        Ok(0) => 0,
        Ok(_) => 0,
        Err(err) => {
            eprintln!("mas-api: {err}");
            2
        },
    });
}

async fn run() -> Result<i32, String> {
    let dev_inmemory = std::env::args().skip(1).any(|arg| arg == "--dev-inmemory");

    let layered = mas_common::config::load_layered().map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    let merger = mas_common::config::Merger::new(&layered);
    let http_addr = parse_addr_value(
        merger.string(
            "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
            "server.http_addr",
            &ServerConfig::default().http_addr.to_string(),
        ),
        "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
    )?;
    let grpc_addr = parse_addr_value(
        merger.string(
            "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
            "server.grpc_addr",
            &ServerConfig::default().grpc_addr.to_string(),
        ),
        "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
    )?;
    let _ = (&http_addr, &grpc_addr); // listener bind-up ships with compose path below

    // Production guardrails (dev flags are exactly the ones documented in
    // config/production.toml's header).
    if environment_string(&merger) == "production" {
        enforce_production_guardrails(&merger.string("MAS_DEV_TOKENS", "server.dev_tokens", ""))?;
    }

    let (tenancy, agents, workflows, executions, schedules, verifier, health) = if dev_inmemory {
        compose_inmemory(&merger)?
    } else {
        compose_production(&merger).await?
    };

    // ── Production-mode guardrails: dev affordances are forbidden even
    //    outside `environment == "production"` — non-dev wiring is always
    //    durable and must never accept static tokens. ──────────────────
    if !dev_inmemory {
        enforce_production_guardrails(&merger.string("MAS_DEV_TOKENS", "server.dev_tokens", ""))?;
    }

    let state = AppState::new(
        "mas-api",
        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        verifier,
        tenancy,
        agents,
        workflows,
        executions,
        schedules,
        health,
    );

    let (http_addr, grpc_addr) = (
        parse_addr_value(
            merger.string(
                "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
                "server.http_addr",
                &ServerConfig::default().http_addr.to_string(),
            ),
            "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
        )?,
        parse_addr_value(
            merger.string(
                "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
                "server.grpc_addr",
                &ServerConfig::default().grpc_addr.to_string(),
            ),
            "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
        )?,
    );

    eprintln!(
        "mas-api starting mode={} http={http_addr} grpc={grpc_addr}",
        if dev_inmemory {
            "--dev-inmemory"
        } else {
            "production"
        }
    );
    mas_api::server::serve(
        state,
        ServerConfig {
            http_addr,
            grpc_addr,
        },
    )
    .await
    .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
    Ok(0)
}

type ServiceSet = (
    Arc<TenancyService>,
    Arc<AgentService>,
    Arc<WorkflowService>,
    Arc<ExecutionService>,
    Arc<ScheduleService>,
    Arc<dyn mas_api::auth::TokenVerifierPort>,
    Arc<HealthRegistry>,
);

fn compose_inmemory(merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>) -> Result<ServiceSet, String> {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryServices::new());
    let audit = Arc::new(InMemoryAuditSink::new());
    let tenancy = Arc::new(TenancyService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
    ));
    let agents = Arc::new(AgentService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
    ));
    let workflows = Arc::new(WorkflowService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
    ));
    let executions = Arc::new(ExecutionService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
        Arc::new(mas_application::durable_memory::InMemoryDurableExecution::new()),
    ));
    let schedules = Arc::new(ScheduleService::new(Box::new(store), Box::new(audit)));
    let _ = merger;

    let verifier: Arc<dyn mas_api::auth::TokenVerifierPort> = Arc::new(dev_verifier()?);
    Ok((
        tenancy,
        agents,
        workflows,
        executions,
        schedules,
        verifier,
        Arc::new(HealthRegistry::new()),
    ))
}

/// Production composition: durable everything, dev affordances rejected.
async fn compose_production(merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>) -> Result<ServiceSet, String> {
    use mas_persistence::pool::{Database, DatabaseUrl, PoolConfig};
    use mas_persistence::repositories::api_keys::ApiKeyStore;
    use mas_persistence::repositories::audit::PostgresAuditLog;
    use mas_persistence::repositories::services::PgServices;
    use mas_persistence::repositories::PgDurableExecution;

    let url = merger.string("MAS_DATABASE_URL", "database.url", "");
    if url.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            "production mode requires a database URL (config database.url or MAS_DATABASE_URL); \
             local bring-up uses --dev-inmemory"
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }
    let max_connections = merger
        .u64("MAS_DATABASE_MAX_CONNS", "database.max_connections", 32)
        .map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    let url_holder = DatabaseUrl::new(url).map_err(|err| format!("database url: {err}"))?;
    let mut config = PoolConfig::for_url(url_holder, "mas-api")
        .map_err(|err| format!("database config: {err}"))?;
    config.max_connections = u32::try_from(max_connections).unwrap_or(32);
    let config = config
        .validated()
        .map_err(|err| format!("database config: {err}"))?;
    let database = Database::connect(&config)
        .await
        .map_err(|err| format!("database: {err}"))?;

    // ── Migration ledger verification (migrate-on-boot is opt-in) ─────
    let pool = database.pool().clone();
    let runner = mas_persistence::migrations::MigrationRunner::new(pool.clone());
    runner
        .ensure_table()
        .await
        .map_err(|err| format!("migrations: {err}"))?;
    let migrate_on_boot = merger
        .bool(
            "MAS_DATABASE_MIGRATE_ON_BOOT",
            "database.migrate_on_boot",
            false,
        )
        .map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    if migrate_on_boot {
        let applied = runner
            .migrate()
            .await
            .map_err(|err| format!("migrate: {err}"))?;
        eprintln!("mas-api: {} migration(s) applied on boot", applied.len());
    } else {
        runner.verify().await.map_err(|err| {
            format!(
                "migration ledger drift — apply migrations first (scripts/migrate.sh up): {err}"
            )
        })?;
    }

    // ── Durable ports (each Box owns a cheap pool handle clone) ───────
    let tenancy = Arc::new(TenancyService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(pool.clone())),
    ));
    let agents = Arc::new(AgentService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(pool.clone())),
    ));
    let workflows = Arc::new(WorkflowService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(pool.clone())),
    ));
    // The durable port is Postgres: submission, claiming, settlement and
    // cancellation all run as one transaction each against the same pool the
    // rest of the service uses.
    let executions = Arc::new(ExecutionService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(pool.clone())),
        Arc::new(PgDurableExecution::new(pool.clone())),
    ));
    let schedules = Arc::new(ScheduleService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(pool.clone())),
    ));

    let verifier: Arc<dyn mas_api::auth::TokenVerifierPort> = Arc::new(
        mas_api::prod_auth::PostgresApiKeyVerifier::new(ApiKeyStore::new(pool.clone())),
    );

    // ── Dependency probe over the same pool ───────────────────────────
    let health = Arc::new(HealthRegistry::new());
    health
        .register(
            mas_observability::health::ProbeKind::Readiness,
            "postgres",
            PgHealthCheck {
                database: database.clone(),
            },
        )
        .map_err(|err| format!("health: {err}"))?;

    Ok((
        tenancy, agents, workflows, executions, schedules, verifier, health,
    ))
}

/// Readiness adapter over the pool's `SELECT 1` probe.
struct PgHealthCheck {
    database: mas_persistence::pool::Database,
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl mas_observability::health::HealthCheckPort for PgHealthCheck {
    async fn check(
        &self,
        at: &mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp,
    ) -> mas_observability::health::ComponentHealth {
        let probe = self.database.probe().await;
        if probe.healthy {
            mas_observability::health::ComponentHealth::up("postgres", at)
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| unreachable!("static name"))
        } else {
            mas_observability::health::ComponentHealth::down(
                "postgres",
                at,
                probe.message.as_deref().unwrap_or("database probe failed"),
            )
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| unreachable!("static name"))
        }
    }
}

/// The production-mode dev-token guardrail, isolated as a pure rule so the
/// binary's test suite pins the exact failure contract: any non-empty
/// `server.dev_tokens` value is refused whenever the process is not
/// explicitly running with `--dev-inmemory`.
fn enforce_production_guardrails(dev_tokens_raw: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    mas_common::config::refuse_if(
        !dev_tokens_raw.trim().is_empty(),
        "production refuses static dev tokens (config server.dev_tokens must stay empty)",
    )
    .map_err(|err| format!("config guardrail: {err}"))
}

fn parse_addr_value(raw: String, source: &str) -> Result<SocketAddr, String> {
    raw.parse()
        .map_err(|err| format!("{source} invalid ('{raw}'): {err}"))
}

/// Effective `environment` key (MAS_ENV wins via the merger's env layer).
fn environment_string(merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>) -> String {
    merger
        .string("MAS_ENV", "environment", "development")
        .to_ascii_lowercase()
}

fn dev_verifier() -> Result<StaticTokenVerifier, String> {
    let layered = mas_common::config::load_layered().map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    let merger = mas_common::config::Merger::new(&layered);
    let mut verifier = StaticTokenVerifier::new().with_token(
        "dev-token",
        uuid::Uuid::now_v7().to_string().as_str(),
        PrincipalKind::User,
    );
    let table = merger.string("MAS_DEV_TOKENS", "server.dev_tokens", "");
    if !table.is_empty() {
        for entry in table.split(',').filter(|e| !e.trim().is_empty()) {
            let mut parts = entry.splitn(3, ':');
            let (Some(token), Some(subject), Some(kind)) =
                (parts.next(), parts.next(), parts.next())
            else {
                return Err(format!(
                    "MAS_DEV_TOKENS entry '{entry}' malformed (token:subject:kind)"
                ));
            };
            let kind = match kind {
                "user" => PrincipalKind::User,
                "service" => PrincipalKind::Service,
                "api_key" => PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
                other => return Err(format!("unknown principal kind '{other}'")),
            };
            verifier = verifier.with_token(token, subject, kind);
        }
    }
    Ok(verifier)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn production_guardrail_accepts_empty_dev_tokens() {
        assert!(enforce_production_guardrails("").is_ok());
        assert!(enforce_production_guardrails("   ").is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn production_guardrail_refuses_configured_dev_tokens() {
        let err = enforce_production_guardrails("dev-token:sub-a:user")
            .expect_err("static tokens must not survive production mode");
        assert!(err.contains("dev tokens"), "message names the cause: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("guardrail"), "message names the gate: {err}");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! PURPOSE: Process state shared by every handler — the application services,
//! the token verifier, the health registry and build identity.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge).
//!
//! Production responsibility: build the object graph exactly once at bootstrap
//! and share it `Arc`-wise, so there is one instance of each service per
//! process and no per-request construction cost or per-request divergence.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • hold per-request or per-tenant mutable state (that belongs on the
//!     request extensions / service context);
//!   • expose a constructor that silently substitutes an in-memory store when
//!     the production store is unavailable.

//! Process state shared by every handler: the five application services
//! (Arc-shared, since they own boxed store ports), the token verifier, the
//! health registry, and build identity. Constructed ONCE at bootstrap.

use std::sync::Arc;

use mas_application::agent_service::AgentService;
use mas_application::execution_service::ExecutionService;
use mas_application::schedule_service::ScheduleService;
use mas_application::tenancy_service::TenancyService;
use mas_application::workflow_service::WorkflowService;
use mas_observability::health::HealthRegistry;

use crate::auth::TokenVerifierPort;

/// Everything a request may touch.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct AppState {
    /// Deployment/service identity for health + logs.
    pub service_name: Arc<str>,
    /// Crate/binary version for health payloads.
    pub service_version: Arc<str>,
    /// Bearer-token verification boundary.
    pub verifier: Arc<dyn TokenVerifierPort>,
    /// Tenancy/identity use-cases.
    pub tenancy: Arc<TenancyService>,
    /// Agent lifecycle use-cases.
    pub agents: Arc<AgentService>,
    /// Workflow lifecycle use-cases.
    pub workflows: Arc<WorkflowService>,
    /// Execution lifecycle use-cases.
    pub executions: Arc<ExecutionService>,
    /// Schedule lifecycle use-cases.
    pub schedules: Arc<ScheduleService>,
    /// Liveness/readiness probes (observability plane).
    pub health: Arc<HealthRegistry>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for AppState {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("AppState")
            .field("service_name", &self.service_name)
            .field("service_version", &self.service_version)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl AppState {
    /// Composition root (services arrive fully wired).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        service_name: &str,
        service_version: &str,
        verifier: Arc<dyn TokenVerifierPort>,
        tenancy: Arc<TenancyService>,
        agents: Arc<AgentService>,
        workflows: Arc<WorkflowService>,
        executions: Arc<ExecutionService>,
        schedules: Arc<ScheduleService>,
        health: Arc<HealthRegistry>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            service_name: service_name.into(),
            service_version: service_version.into(),
            verifier,
            tenancy,
            agents,
            workflows,
            executions,
            schedules,
            health,
        }
    }
}

/// Shared in-memory wiring for this crate's tests (and any downstream
/// handler tests): all services over ONE `InMemoryServices` +
/// `InMemoryAuditSink`, plus a `StaticTokenVerifier` with `test-token`.
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testutils"))]
pub mod test_support {
    use std::sync::Arc;

    use mas_application::agent_service::AgentService;
    use mas_application::audit::InMemoryAuditSink;
    use mas_application::durable_memory::InMemoryDurableExecution;
    use mas_application::execution_service::ExecutionService;
    use mas_application::schedule_service::ScheduleService;
    use mas_application::stores::InMemoryServices;
    use mas_application::tenancy_service::TenancyService;
    use mas_application::workflow_service::WorkflowService;
    use mas_observability::health::HealthRegistry;

    use super::AppState;
    use crate::auth::{PrincipalKind, StaticTokenVerifier};

    /// Fresh, fully-wired state over one shared in-memory store.
    pub fn inmemory_state() -> AppState {
        let store = Arc::new(InMemoryServices::new());
        let audit = Arc::new(InMemoryAuditSink::new());
        let tenancy = Arc::new(TenancyService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
        ));
        let agents = Arc::new(AgentService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
        ));
        let workflows = Arc::new(WorkflowService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
        ));
        // The durable port is mandatory. The in-memory implementation is
        // accepted here only because this is the crate's test harness — the
        // production composition root wires `PgDurableExecution`.
        let durable = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
        let executions = Arc::new(ExecutionService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
            durable,
        ));
        let schedules = Arc::new(ScheduleService::new(Box::new(store), Box::new(audit)));
        let verifier = Arc::new(StaticTokenVerifier::new().with_token(
            "test-token",
            &uuid::Uuid::now_v7().to_string(),
            PrincipalKind::User,
        ));
        AppState::new(
            "mas-api-test",
            env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
            verifier,
            tenancy,
            agents,
            workflows,
            executions,
            schedules,
            Arc::new(HealthRegistry::new()),
        )
    }
}
```

**PURPOSE:**

```text
The `mas-application` crate manifest.

Owning layer: `mas-application`.

Production responsibility: declare the use-case layer's dependencies,
including `mas-observability` for the named pipeline metrics and the safe
structured-log surface, and `mas-events` for the canonical event builder.

It must NOT:
• depend on a process crate (`mas-api`, `mas-worker`,
`mas-scheduler-service`) — the dependency points the other way;
• depend on `mas-persistence`; persistence implements this crate's ports;
• take a concrete infrastructure dependency where a port will do.
```

```toml
# PURPOSE: The `mas-application` crate manifest.
#
# Owning layer: `mas-application`.
#
# Production responsibility: declare the use-case layer's dependencies,
# including `mas-observability` for the named pipeline metrics and the safe
# structured-log surface, and `mas-events` for the canonical event builder.
#
# It must NOT:
#   • depend on a process crate (`mas-api`, `mas-worker`,
#     `mas-scheduler-service`) — the dependency points the other way;
#   • depend on `mas-persistence`; persistence implements this crate's ports;
#   • take a concrete infrastructure dependency where a port will do.

[package]
name = "mas-application"
description = "Use-case services composing domain and infrastructure ports; internal DTO mapping."
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
publish = false

[dependencies]
mas-common = { workspace = true }
mas-domain = { workspace = true }
mas-contracts = { workspace = true }
# mas-events is pulled in because the durable submission units of work write
# their domain events into the transactional outbox *inside the same
# transaction* as the state change. mas-events depends only on
# common/domain/orchestration, so this adds no dependency cycle.
mas-events = { workspace = true }
# mas-observability is pulled in for the named pipeline metrics: the durable
# pipeline's counters must be declared once, in the crate every emitting layer
# already depends on.
mas-observability = { workspace = true }
async-trait = { workspace = true }
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
tracing = { workspace = true }
sha2 = { workspace = true }
hex = { workspace = true }
uuid = { workspace = true }
chrono = { workspace = true }

[dev-dependencies]
criterion = { version = "0.5", features = ["html_reports"] }
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt", "time"] }

[lints]
workspace = true

[[bench]]
name = "root_topological_bench"
path = "../../benches/topological_bench.rs"
harness = false
```
