### FILE: `enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/application/src/tenant_isolation.rs`

**PURPOSE:**

```text
The multi-tenant isolation suite for the canonical durable
execution pipeline: one executed proof per way one tenant must NOT be able
to touch another tenant's run.

Owning layer: `mas-application` (the canonical durable port). Every test
here targets the port the HTTP/API layer calls, so what is proven here is
what a request can actually reach.

Production responsibility: tenancy in this system is enforced by scoping,
not by filtering. A foreign tenant's execution must read as *absent* —
`None`, not `Forbidden` — because existence itself is information, and a
"not found" that leaks that row 42 belongs to someone else is a disclosure.
These tests pin that distinction, plus the seven guarantees the spec names:
tenant B must not read, claim, execute, cancel, receive the result of,
receive the events of, or receive the usage of tenant A's execution.

The database-level half of this suite lives next to the SQL that implements
it, in `crates/persistence/tests/tenant_sql_contract.rs`, which asserts that
every durable statement carries a tenant predicate. The two halves are the
same guarantee seen from the two ends: this file proves the *behaviour*,
that file proves the *statements* cannot be written any other way.

It must NOT:
• assert `Forbidden` where `NotFound` is required — a test that accepts
either is a test that permits an existence oracle;
• scope anything by a value the caller supplies after the fact; the tenant
is part of the query, never a post-filter;
• weaken, skip or delete the existing Python tenant-isolation tests. Those
are untouched by this work and remain the cross-service half of the
guarantee.
```

```rust
// PURPOSE: The multi-tenant isolation suite for the canonical durable
// execution pipeline: one executed proof per way one tenant must NOT be able
// to touch another tenant's run.
//
// Owning layer: `mas-application` (the canonical durable port). Every test
// here targets the port the HTTP/API layer calls, so what is proven here is
// what a request can actually reach.
//
// Production responsibility: tenancy in this system is enforced by scoping,
// not by filtering. A foreign tenant's execution must read as *absent* —
// `None`, not `Forbidden` — because existence itself is information, and a
// "not found" that leaks that row 42 belongs to someone else is a disclosure.
// These tests pin that distinction, plus the seven guarantees the spec names:
// tenant B must not read, claim, execute, cancel, receive the result of,
// receive the events of, or receive the usage of tenant A's execution.
//
// The database-level half of this suite lives next to the SQL that implements
// it, in `crates/persistence/tests/tenant_sql_contract.rs`, which asserts that
// every durable statement carries a tenant predicate. The two halves are the
// same guarantee seen from the two ends: this file proves the *behaviour*,
// that file proves the *statements* cannot be written any other way.
//
// It must NOT:
//   • assert `Forbidden` where `NotFound` is required — a test that accepts
//     either is a test that permits an existence oracle;
//   • scope anything by a value the caller supplies after the fact; the tenant
//     is part of the query, never a post-filter;
//   • weaken, skip or delete the existing Python tenant-isolation tests. Those
//     are untouched by this work and remain the cross-service half of the
//     guarantee.

#![cfg(test)]

use mas_common::enums::{ExecutionStatus, TaskPriority, TaskStatus};
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId, WorkflowId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_domain::TransitionActor;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::durable::{
    CancellationRequest, ClaimQuery, DurableExecutionPort, ExecutionUsage, SubmissionIntent,
    TaskOutcome, TaskSettlement,
};
use crate::durable_memory::InMemoryDurableExecution;
use crate::fingerprint::{FingerprintInput, RequestFingerprint};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Two tenants, side by side
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Tenant A: owns everything the tests protect.
fn tenant_a() -> TenantId {
    TenantId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(0xA_A_A_A))
}

/// Tenant B: the attacker. It has a valid principal, valid credentials, and no
/// relationship whatsoever to A's work.
fn tenant_b() -> TenantId {
    TenantId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(0xB_B_B_B))
}

fn now(offset: u64) -> Timestamp {
    Timestamp::from_unix_seconds(1_700_000_000 + i64::try_from(offset).expect("fits"))
        .expect("fixed timestamp")
}

/// One submission for `tenant`, keyed by `key`.
fn intent(tenant: TenantId, key: &str) -> SubmissionIntent {
    let input = serde_json::json!({"job": key});
    let organization_id = OrganizationId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(1));
    let project_id = ProjectId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(2));
    let workflow_id = WorkflowId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(3));
    let fingerprint = RequestFingerprint::submission(&FingerprintInput {
        tenant_id: tenant,
        organization_id,
        project_id,
        workflow_id: Some(workflow_id),
        agent_id: None,
        operation: "execution.run",
        input: &input,
        priority: TaskPriority::Normal,
        deadline: None,
    })
    .expect("fingerprint");
    SubmissionIntent {
        tenant_id: tenant,
        organization_id,
        project_id,
        workflow_id: Some(workflow_id),
        agent_id: None,
        input,
        idempotency_key: Some(key.to_owned()),
        fingerprint,
        operation: "execution.run".to_owned(),
        priority: TaskPriority::Normal,
        max_attempts: 3,
        deadline: None,
        correlation_id: format!("corr-{key}"),
        created_by: "user-1".to_owned(),
        actor: TransitionActor::principal("user-1", tenant).expect("actor"),
        create_initial_attempt: false,
        now: now(0),
    }
}

/// Submits one execution for each tenant and returns both receipts.
async fn two_tenants(
    store: &Arc<InMemoryDurableExecution>,
) -> (
    crate::durable::SubmissionReceipt,
    crate::durable::SubmissionReceipt,
) {
    let a = store
        .submit(intent(tenant_a(), "a-key"))
        .await
        .expect("submit a");
    let b = store
        .submit(intent(tenant_b(), "b-key"))
        .await
        .expect("submit b");
    (a, b)
}

/// Reads a task, which is the shape every worker and API read takes.
async fn load(
    store: &Arc<InMemoryDurableExecution>,
    tenant: TenantId,
    task: mas_common::ids::TaskId,
) -> Result<Option<(mas_domain::Task, Option<mas_domain::Execution>)>> {
    store.load_task(tenant, task).await
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. Tenant B must not READ tenant A's execution
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_read_tenant_a_execution() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;
    let execution_id = a.execution.id;

    // The owner reads it.
    assert!(
        store
            .load_execution(tenant_a(), execution_id)
            .await
            .expect("read")
            .is_some(),
        "tenant A can read its own execution"
    );

    // Tenant B gets *absence*, and specifically not a permission error: the
    // point is that B cannot even learn the row exists.
    let foreign = store
        .load_execution(tenant_b(), execution_id)
        .await
        .expect("read");
    assert!(
        foreign.is_none(),
        "existence is hidden across tenants, not merely forbidden"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_listing_never_contains_tenant_a_executions() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    let listed_b = store.list_executions(tenant_b(), 100).await.expect("list");
    assert_eq!(listed_b.len(), 1, "tenant B sees exactly its own execution");
    assert_eq!(listed_b[0].id, b.execution.id);
    assert!(
        listed_b
            .iter()
            .all(|execution| execution.tenant_id == tenant_b()),
        "no foreign row can appear in a tenant-scoped listing"
    );

    let listed_a = store.list_executions(tenant_a(), 100).await.expect("list");
    assert_eq!(listed_a.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(listed_a[0].id, a.execution.id);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_load_tenant_a_task() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    assert!(
        load(&store, tenant_a(), a.task.id)
            .await
            .expect("read")
            .is_some(),
        "tenant A can load its own task"
    );
    assert!(
        load(&store, tenant_b(), a.task.id)
            .await
            .expect("read")
            .is_none(),
        "tenant B cannot load tenant A's task — the task carries no tenant of its own,\
         so it must be read through its execution's scope"
    );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. Tenant B must not CLAIM (and therefore not execute) tenant A's work
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_claim_tenant_a_task() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    let claim = store
        .claim(ClaimQuery {
            worker: "worker-b".to_owned(),
            capacity: 10,
            lease_until: now(30),
            now: now(1),
            tenant_id: Some(tenant_b()),
            task_id: Some(a.task.id),
        })
        .await
        .expect("claim");

    assert!(
        claim.is_empty(),
        "a tenant-scoped claim cannot reach another tenant's task"
    );

    // And the task is untouched by the attempt.
    let (row, _) = load(&store, tenant_a(), a.task.id)
        .await
        .expect("read")
        .expect("row");
    assert_eq!(row.status, TaskStatus::Queued);
    assert_eq!(
        row.locked_by, None,
        "no ownership was granted to tenant B's worker"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_tenant_scoped_claim_only_ever_returns_that_tenants_tasks() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    for tenant in [tenant_a(), tenant_b()] {
        let claimed = store
            .claim(ClaimQuery {
                worker: format!("worker-{tenant}"),
                capacity: 100,
                lease_until: now(30),
                now: now(1),
                tenant_id: Some(tenant),
                task_id: None,
            })
            .await
            .expect("claim");
        assert_eq!(claimed.len(), 1, "each tenant claims exactly its own task");
        let expected = if tenant == tenant_a() {
            a.task.id
        } else {
            b.task.id
        };
        assert_eq!(claimed[0].task.id, expected);
        assert_eq!(claimed[0].task.tenant_id, tenant);
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_renew_a_lease_on_tenant_a_task() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    // Tenant A's worker owns the task.
    let owned = store
        .claim(ClaimQuery {
            worker: "worker-a".to_owned(),
            capacity: 1,
            lease_until: now(30),
            now: now(1),
            tenant_id: Some(tenant_a()),
            task_id: Some(a.task.id),
        })
        .await
        .expect("claim");
    assert_eq!(owned.len(), 1);

    // Tenant B tries to keep that lease alive — a step towards running the work.
    let renewed = store
        .renew_lease(a.task.id, "worker-b", now(120))
        .await
        .expect("renew");
    assert!(
        !renewed,
        "a foreign worker cannot extend a lease it does not own"
    );
    assert!(
        store
            .renew_lease(a.task.id, "worker-a", now(120))
            .await
            .expect("renew"),
        "the owning worker can"
    );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. Tenant B must not SETTLE (produce the result of) tenant A's task
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_settle_tenant_a_task() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    // Tenant A's worker owns the task and has an attempt.
    let owned = store
        .claim(ClaimQuery {
            worker: "worker-a".to_owned(),
            capacity: 1,
            lease_until: now(30),
            now: now(1),
            tenant_id: Some(tenant_a()),
            task_id: Some(a.task.id),
        })
        .await
        .expect("claim");
    let claim = &owned[0];

    // Tenant B tries to settle it as a success — the shortest path from "no
    // access" to "a result the owner will be billed for".
    let forged = store
        .settle(TaskSettlement {
            tenant_id: tenant_b(),
            task_id: a.task.id,
            attempt_id: claim.attempt.id,
            worker: "worker-b".to_owned(),
            expected_version: claim.task.version,
            outcome: TaskOutcome::Succeeded {
                usage: ExecutionUsage {
                    provider: Some("openai".to_owned()),
                    model: Some("gpt-4o-mini".to_owned()),
                    tokens_input: 1_000_000,
                    tokens_output: 1_000_000,
                    tool_calls: 0,
                    steps: 1,
                    cost_micros: Some(999_999),
                },
            },
            execution: None,
            actor: TransitionActor::principal("attacker", tenant_b()).expect("actor"),
            now: now(2),
        })
        .await;

    assert!(
        forged.is_err(),
        "tenant B must not be able to write a result onto tenant A's task"
    );
    assert!(
        store.usage().is_empty(),
        "and no usage was metered to tenant A by that forged settlement"
    );

    // Tenant A's task is exactly as it was.
    let (row, _) = load(&store, tenant_a(), a.task.id)
        .await
        .expect("read")
        .expect("row");
    assert_eq!(row.status, TaskStatus::Running);
    assert_eq!(row.locked_by.as_deref(), Some("worker-a"));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. Tenant B must not CANCEL tenant A's execution
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_cancel_tenant_a_execution() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;
    let execution_id = a.execution.id;

    let cancelled = store
        .cancel(CancellationRequest {
            tenant_id: tenant_b(),
            execution_id,
            actor: TransitionActor::principal("attacker", tenant_b()).expect("actor"),
            correlation_id: "corr-attack".to_owned(),
            now: now(1),
        })
        .await;

    match cancelled {
        Ok(_) => panic!("tenant B must not be able to cancel tenant A's execution"),
        Err(error) => assert!(
            matches!(error, AppError::NotFound { .. }),
            "the refusal must be NotFound, not Forbidden: a Forbidden would confirm the \
             execution exists and belongs to someone else. Got: {error:?}"
        ),
    }

    // Tenant A's execution is untouched.
    let execution = store
        .load_execution(tenant_a(), execution_id)
        .await
        .expect("read")
        .expect("row");
    assert_eq!(execution.status, ExecutionStatus::Queued);
    assert!(!execution.cancellation_requested());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_transition_tenant_a_execution() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    // A bare tenant-B transition attempt on A's execution must fail. The
    // concrete action does not matter: the tenant scope is what is tested.
    let attempted = store
        .transition(crate::durable::ExecutionTransitionRequest {
            tenant_id: tenant_b(),
            execution_id: a.execution.id,
            action: crate::durable::ExecutionAction::Complete,
            actor: TransitionActor::principal("attacker", tenant_b()).expect("actor"),
            correlation_id: "corr-attack".to_owned(),
            now: now(1),
        })
        .await;

    assert!(
        attempted.is_err(),
        "tenant B cannot move tenant A's execution through the lifecycle"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        store
            .load_execution(tenant_a(), a.execution.id)
            .await
            .expect("read")
            .expect("row")
            .status,
        ExecutionStatus::Queued
    );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 5. Tenant B must not receive tenant A's EVENTS
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[tokio::test]
async fn every_event_carries_the_tenant_it_belongs_to() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, b) = two_tenants(&store).await;
    let b_execution_id = b.execution.id;

    // Events are published with a tenant on the envelope, so a consumer — or a
    // subject filter — can never mistake one tenant's stream for another's.
    for row in store.outbox() {
        assert!(
            row.envelope.tenant_id == tenant_a() || row.envelope.tenant_id == tenant_b(),
            "an event with no tenant cannot be routed safely"
        );
    }

    let b_events: Vec<_> = store
        .outbox()
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|row| row.envelope.tenant_id == tenant_b())
        .collect();
    assert!(!b_events.is_empty(), "tenant B's own events exist");
    assert!(
        b_events.iter().all(
            |row| row.envelope.aggregate_id == b_execution_id.to_string()
                || row.envelope.tenant_id == tenant_b()
        ),
        "tenant B's events describe tenant B's aggregates"
    );

    // Tenant A's execution never appears in tenant B's event stream.
    assert!(
        b_events
            .iter()
            .all(|row| row.envelope.aggregate_id != a.execution.id.to_string()),
        "no event about tenant A's execution is addressed to tenant B"
    );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 6. Tenant B must not receive (or be charged for) tenant A's USAGE
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[tokio::test]
async fn usage_is_attributable_to_the_tenant_that_did_the_work() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    // Tenant A's worker runs its task to completion.
    let owned = store
        .claim(ClaimQuery {
            worker: "worker-a".to_owned(),
            capacity: 1,
            lease_until: now(30),
            now: now(1),
            tenant_id: Some(tenant_a()),
            task_id: Some(a.task.id),
        })
        .await
        .expect("claim");
    let claim = &owned[0];

    let receipt = store
        .settle(TaskSettlement {
            tenant_id: tenant_a(),
            task_id: a.task.id,
            attempt_id: claim.attempt.id,
            worker: "worker-a".to_owned(),
            expected_version: claim.task.version,
            outcome: TaskOutcome::Succeeded {
                usage: ExecutionUsage {
                    provider: Some("openai".to_owned()),
                    model: Some("gpt-4o-mini".to_owned()),
                    tokens_input: 100,
                    tokens_output: 20,
                    tool_calls: 1,
                    steps: 2,
                    cost_micros: Some(1_500),
                },
            },
            execution: Some(crate::durable::ExecutionFinalization {
                execution_id: a.execution.id,
                outcome: crate::durable::ExecutionOutcome::Completed,
            }),
            actor: TransitionActor::principal("worker-a", tenant_a()).expect("actor"),
            now: now(2),
        })
        .await
        .expect("settle");

    assert!(
        !receipt.usage.is_empty(),
        "a successful run is metered — usage comes from what was consumed, not a counter"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        receipt.execution.as_ref().expect("execution").tenant_id,
        tenant_a(),
        "the finalized execution is tenant A's"
    );

    // Tenant B's listing, counters and reads are unaffected by A's success.
    let listed_b = store.list_executions(tenant_b(), 100).await.expect("list");
    assert_eq!(
        listed_b.len(),
        1,
        "tenant B's view of its own work is unchanged by tenant A's activity"
    );
    assert!(
        listed_b
            .iter()
            .all(|execution| execution.tenant_id == tenant_b()),
        "tenant B never receives tenant A's result"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn tenant_b_cannot_see_tenant_a_work_in_the_durable_counters() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    // Only tenant A's task is claimable for tenant B's worker? No: the claim
    // is tenant-scoped, so B's worker has nothing. The counters that drive
    // capacity and backlog must reflect that, or a worker would spin.
    let counters = store.counters("worker-b", &now(1)).await.expect("counters");

    let b_claimable = store
        .claim(ClaimQuery {
            worker: "worker-b".to_owned(),
            capacity: 100,
            lease_until: now(30),
            now: now(1),
            tenant_id: Some(tenant_b()),
            task_id: None,
        })
        .await
        .expect("claim");

    assert!(
        counters.claimable_tasks >= 1,
        "tenant A's work is claimable in aggregate ({})",
        counters.claimable_tasks
    );
    assert!(
        b_claimable
            .iter()
            .all(|claim| claim.task.tenant_id == tenant_b()),
        "but never by a tenant-scoped claim for tenant B"
    );
    assert_eq!(b_claimable.len(), 1);
    let _ = a;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 7. Identity is never inferred — it is always carried
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_same_idempotency_key_in_two_tenants_is_two_executions() {
    // Tenant identity is part of the idempotency key's scope. Without this, one
    // tenant could consume another tenant's idempotency key and have its
    // request answered with someone else's execution.
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());

    let a = store
        .submit(intent(tenant_a(), "shared-key"))
        .await
        .expect("submit a");
    let b = store
        .submit(intent(tenant_b(), "shared-key"))
        .await
        .expect("submit b");

    assert_ne!(
        a.execution.id, b.execution.id,
        "one idempotency key, two tenants, two independent executions"
    );
    assert_eq!(a.execution.tenant_id, tenant_a());
    assert_eq!(b.execution.tenant_id, tenant_b());

    // And each tenant's re-submission replays only its own execution.
    let replayed = store
        .submit(intent(tenant_b(), "shared-key"))
        .await
        .expect("replay b");
    assert_eq!(
        replayed.execution.id, b.execution.id,
        "tenant B's replay returns tenant B's execution, never tenant A's"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_task_never_outlives_its_tenant_scope_after_completion() {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
    let (a, _b) = two_tenants(&store).await;

    let owned = store
        .claim(ClaimQuery {
            worker: "worker-a".to_owned(),
            capacity: 1,
            lease_until: now(30),
            now: now(1),
            tenant_id: Some(tenant_a()),
            task_id: Some(a.task.id),
        })
        .await
        .expect("claim");
    let claim = &owned[0];

    store
        .settle(TaskSettlement {
            tenant_id: tenant_a(),
            task_id: a.task.id,
            attempt_id: claim.attempt.id,
            worker: "worker-a".to_owned(),
            expected_version: claim.task.version,
            outcome: TaskOutcome::Succeeded {
                usage: ExecutionUsage::default(),
            },
            execution: Some(crate::durable::ExecutionFinalization {
                execution_id: a.execution.id,
                outcome: crate::durable::ExecutionOutcome::Completed,
            }),
            actor: TransitionActor::principal("worker-a", tenant_a()).expect("actor"),
            now: now(2),
        })
        .await
        .expect("settle");

    // The finished execution is readable by its owner and invisible to B.
    let finished = store
        .load_execution(tenant_a(), a.execution.id)
        .await
        .expect("read")
        .expect("row");
    assert_eq!(finished.status, ExecutionStatus::Completed);
    assert!(
        store
            .load_execution(tenant_b(), a.execution.id)
            .await
            .expect("read")
            .is_none(),
        "completion does not widen the visibility of the row"
    );
}

/// The lease window a worker gets: long enough to be useful, short enough that
/// a crashed worker's task is reclaimed promptly. Referenced here so the
/// isolation suite reads as one file.
const _LEASE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
```

**PURPOSE:**

_PURPOSE ব্লক এই ফাইলের হেডারে নেই; ফাইলটি জেনারেটেড বা কনফিগারেশন-মাত্র._

```rust
//! PURPOSE: The shared state enums whose string values are the platform's wire
//! contract.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-common` (the base layer).
//!
//! Production responsibility: one definition of every status, priority and
//! class, with a stable `snake_case` representation shared by database rows,
//! events, API payloads and metrics labels. Renaming a shipped variant is a
//! breaking change to all four.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • rename or renumber a variant once shipped;
//!   • carry domain behaviour — these are vocabulary, not logic;
//!   • gain an `Other`/`Unknown` catch-all that lets a real state go unnamed.

//! Shared state enums used across crates.
//!
//! Every enum has a *stable* wire representation: `snake_case` strings via
//! serde, `as_str` / `Display` and `FromStr`. The string values are
//! part of the platform contract (database rows, events, API payloads) and
//! must never be renamed once shipped.

/// Defines a string-representable enum with the full standard surface:
/// `as_str`, `Display`, `FromStr` (accepting only canonical strings),
/// `ALL` (all variants), serde as `snake_case` strings, and `variant_names`.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! string_enum {
    (
        $(#[$meta:meta])*
        $name:ident {
            $( $(#[$vmeta:meta])* $variant:ident => $str:literal ),+ $(,)?
        }
    ) => {
        $(#[$meta])*
        #[derive(
            Debug,
            Clone,
            Copy,
            PartialEq,
            Eq,
            Hash,
            PartialOrd,
            Ord,
            ::serde::Serialize,
            ::serde::Deserialize,
        )]
        #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
        pub enum $name {
            $( $(#[$vmeta])* $variant ),+
        }

        impl $name {
            /// Every variant, in declaration order.
            pub const ALL: &'static [Self] = &[ $( Self::$variant ),+ ];

            /// Canonical stable string representation (matches serde output).
            #[must_use]
            pub const fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
                match self {
                    $( Self::$variant => $str ),+
                }
            }

            /// All canonical string values, in declaration order.
            #[must_use]
            pub const fn variant_names() -> &'static [&'static str] {
                &[ $( $str ),+ ]
            }
        }

        impl ::std::fmt::Display for $name {
            fn fmt(&self, f: &mut ::std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> ::std::fmt::Result {
                f.write_str(self.as_str())
            }
        }

        impl ::std::str::FromStr for $name {
            type Err = $crate::error::AppError;

            fn from_str(s: &str) -> ::std::result::Result<Self, Self::Err> {
                match s.trim() {
                    $( $str => ::std::result::Result::Ok(Self::$variant), )+
                    other => ::std::result::Result::Err($crate::error::AppError::Validation {
                        message: ::std::format!(
                            "invalid {}: {:?} (expected one of: {})",
                            ::std::stringify!($name),
                            other,
                            <[::std::string::String]>::join(
                                &[ $( ::std::string::String::from($str) ),+ ],
                                ", ",
                            ),
                        ),
                        issues: ::std::vec![$crate::error::ValidationIssue::new(
                            ::std::stringify!($name),
                            "invalid_enum_value",
                            "unknown enum value; see message for the allowed set",
                        )],
                    }),
                }
            }
        }

        impl ::std::convert::AsRef<str> for $name {
            fn as_ref(&self) -> &str {
                self.as_str()
            }
        }
    };
}
```

### FILE: `enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/common/src/error.rs`

**PURPOSE:**

_PURPOSE ব্লক এই ফাইলের হেডারে নেই; ফাইলটি জেনারেটেড বা কনফিগারেশন-মাত্র._

```rust
//! PURPOSE: The unified, transport-agnostic error model every crate converges
//! on.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-common` (the base layer).
//!
//! Production responsibility: one taxonomy that carries a stable machine
//! code, a *safe* public message and an HTTP mapping, so the API boundary can
//! translate without leaking internals, and the worker can classify retry
//! vs terminal from the variant itself.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • put a credential, token, payload or connection string in a message —
//!     `public_message()` must stay safe to return to a caller;
//!   • add a variant without adding it to the exhaustive classifier in
//!     `mas-worker::classify`, which would inherit the wrong retry class;
//!   • collapse distinct failures into one generic internal error.

//! Unified, transport-agnostic error model.
//!
//! Every crate converges on [`AppError`]. The API/gRPC boundary converts it
//! into the stable external contract (`StableApiError` in `mas-contracts`)
//! using only [`AppError::error_code`], [`AppError::public_message`] and
//! [`AppError::http_status`], so internal details never leak.

use http::StatusCode;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::time::Duration;

/// Machine-readable detail about a single invalid field or rule violation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ValidationIssue {
    /// Name or dotted path of the offending field.
    pub field: String,
    /// Stable machine-readable rule code (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`).
    pub code: String,
    /// Safe, human-readable explanation.
    pub message: String,
}

impl ValidationIssue {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(
        field: impl Into<String>,
        code: impl Into<String>,
        message: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            field: field.into(),
            code: code.into(),
            message: message.into(),
        }
    }
}

/// The single error type used across `rust-core`.
///
/// Variants are intentionally coarse: fine-grained context travels in the
/// payload strings/structures, never in new variants (keeps error codes stable).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum AppError {
    /// Input failed validation. `issues` carries field-level detail (may be empty).
    #[error("validation failed: {message}")]
    Validation {
        message: String,
        issues: Vec<ValidationIssue>,
    },

    /// Looked-up resource does not exist (or is invisible to the caller).
    #[error("{resource} not found (lookup: {lookup})")]
    NotFound {
        resource: &'static str,
        lookup: String,
    },

    /// Missing/invalid/expired credentials.
    #[error("unauthenticated: {0}")]
    Unauthorized(String),

    /// Authenticated, but not allowed to perform the action.
    #[error("forbidden: {0}")]
    Forbidden(String),

    /// State conflict (duplicate key, illegal transition, optimistic-lock failure).
    #[error("conflict: {0}")]
    Conflict(String),

    /// Quota/rate limit exceeded; retry after the hinted delay.
    #[error("rate limited: {0}")]
    RateLimited(String),

    /// Operation exceeded its deadline.
    #[error("operation timed out: {0}")]
    Timeout(String),

    /// Operation was cancelled by the caller/system before completion.
    #[error("operation cancelled: {0}")]
    Cancelled(String),

    /// Database-layer failure (connection, query, migration, integrity).
    #[error("database error: {0}")]
    Database(String),

    /// Message-broker / queue failure.
    #[error("messaging error: {0}")]
    Messaging(String),

    /// (De)serialization failure of internal payloads.
    #[error("serialization error: {0}")]
    Serialization(String),

    /// An outbound call to an external dependency failed.
    #[error("external service '{service}' failed: {message}")]
    ExternalService { service: String, message: String },

    /// Unexpected internal failure; the payload is never sent to clients.
    #[error("internal error: {0}")]
    Internal(String),

    /// A structured failure an external agent runtime reported.
    ///
    /// This exists because the AI orchestrator has its own error vocabulary
    /// (`rate_limited`, `invalid_tool_permission`, `context_length_exceeded`,
    /// ...) and its own opinion about whether a retry is worth it. Flattening
    /// that into `ExternalService` would discard both: the code would become
    /// `EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR` and every run would look transient, so a
    /// permanently invalid request would burn the whole attempt budget before
    /// it dead-letters.
    ///
    /// The variant carries the external code and message verbatim (already
    /// redacted by the bridge) so the durable failure record and the audit
    /// trail name what actually went wrong.
    #[error("external failure [{code}]: {message}")]
    ExternalFailure {
        /// Stable code the external runtime reported.
        code: String,
        /// Safe, already-redacted message from the external runtime.
        message: String,
        /// Whether the external runtime believes another attempt may succeed.
        retryable: bool,
    },
}

impl AppError {
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Constructors
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Simple validation failure without field detail.
    pub fn validation(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Validation {
            message: message.into(),
            issues: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Validation failure with structured field detail.
    pub fn validation_with_issues(
        message: impl Into<String>,
        issues: Vec<ValidationIssue>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self::Validation {
            message: message.into(),
            issues,
        }
    }

    /// Single-field validation failure convenience.
    pub fn invalid_field(
        field: impl Into<String>,
        code: impl Into<String>,
        message: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Self {
        let issue = ValidationIssue::new(field, code, message);
        Self::Validation {
            message: format!("invalid value for field '{}'", issue.field),
            issues: vec![issue],
        }
    }

    pub fn not_found(resource: &'static str, lookup: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::NotFound {
            resource,
            lookup: lookup.into(),
        }
    }

    pub fn unauthorized(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Unauthorized(message.into())
    }

    pub fn forbidden(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Forbidden(message.into())
    }

    pub fn conflict(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Conflict(message.into())
    }

    pub fn rate_limited(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::RateLimited(message.into())
    }

    pub fn timeout(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Timeout(message.into())
    }

    pub fn cancelled(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled(message.into())
    }

    pub fn database(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Database(message.into())
    }

    pub fn messaging(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Messaging(message.into())
    }

    pub fn serialization(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Serialization(message.into())
    }

    pub fn external_service(service: impl Into<String>, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::ExternalService {
            service: service.into(),
            message: message.into(),
        }
    }

    /// Constructs a structured failure an external agent runtime reported.
    ///
    /// `retryable` is the external runtime's own verdict and is honoured as
    /// given: it produced the failure, so it classified it, and it has more
    /// information about it than this process does.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn external_failure(
        code: impl Into<String>,
        message: impl Into<String>,
        retryable: bool,
    ) -> Self {
        Self::ExternalFailure {
            code: code.into(),
            message: message.into(),
            retryable,
        }
    }

    /// Internal errors wrap debugging context that must never reach clients.
    pub fn internal(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Internal(message.into())
    }

    /// Wrap an internal error with additional context, preserving retryability class.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_context(self, context: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let context = context.into();
        match self {
            Self::Database(m) => Self::Database(format!("{context}: {m}")),
            Self::Messaging(m) => Self::Messaging(format!("{context}: {m}")),
            Self::ExternalService { service, message } => Self::ExternalService {
                service,
                message: format!("{context}: {message}"),
            },
            Self::Internal(m) => Self::Internal(format!("{context}: {m}")),
            Self::Serialization(m) => Self::Serialization(format!("{context}: {m}")),
            other => other,
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Classification
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Stable, externally visible machine code. Part of the API contract —
    /// never rename or repurpose a code once shipped.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn error_code(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Validation { .. } => "VALIDATION_FAILED",
            Self::NotFound { .. } => "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND",
            Self::Unauthorized(_) => "UNAUTHENTICATED",
            Self::Forbidden(_) => "FORBIDDEN",
            Self::Conflict(_) => "CONFLICT",
            Self::RateLimited(_) => "RATE_LIMITED",
            Self::Timeout(_) => "TIMEOUT",
            Self::Cancelled(_) => "CANCELLED",
            Self::Database(_) => "DATABASE_ERROR",
            Self::Messaging(_) => "MESSAGING_ERROR",
            Self::Serialization(_) => "SERIALIZATION_ERROR",
            Self::ExternalService { .. } => "EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR",
            Self::Internal(_) => "INTERNAL_ERROR",
            Self::ExternalFailure { .. } => "EXTERNAL_FAILURE",
        }
    }

    /// Whether the operation may be retried by a caller/worker with backoff.
    /// This classifies *error categories*; per-operation rules (e.g. max
    /// attempts, non-idempotent writes) live in the retry policy layer.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::RateLimited(_) | Self::Timeout(_) | Self::Messaging(_) | Self::Database(_) => {
                true
            },
            Self::ExternalService { .. } => true,
            // The external runtime's own verdict decides; it produced the
            // failure and therefore knows whether a retry can help.
            Self::ExternalFailure { retryable, .. } => *retryable,
            Self::Validation { .. }
            | Self::NotFound { .. }
            | Self::Unauthorized(_)
            | Self::Forbidden(_)
            | Self::Conflict(_)
            | Self::Cancelled(_)
            | Self::Serialization(_)
            | Self::Internal(_) => false,
        }
    }

    /// Suggested delay before retrying, when the error itself carries such a hint.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn retry_after_hint(&self) -> Option<Duration> {
        match self {
            Self::RateLimited(_) => Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
            Self::Timeout(_) => Some(Duration::from_millis(250)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// HTTP status used by the API boundary when mapping this error.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn http_status(&self) -> StatusCode {
        match self {
            Self::Validation { .. } => StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
            Self::NotFound { .. } => StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
            Self::Unauthorized(_) => StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
            Self::Forbidden(_) => StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
            Self::Conflict(_) => StatusCode::CONFLICT,
            Self::RateLimited(_) => StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
            Self::Timeout(_) => StatusCode::GATEWAY_TIMEOUT,
            // 499 (nginx-style "Client Closed Request") is the de-facto
            // cancellation status; fall back to 400 if a stack rejects it.
            Self::Cancelled(_) => StatusCode::from_u16(499).unwrap_or(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST),
            Self::Database(_) | Self::Messaging(_) | Self::Serialization(_) | Self::Internal(_) => {
                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
            },
            Self::ExternalService { .. } => StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
            Self::ExternalFailure { retryable, .. } => {
                if *retryable {
                    StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY
                } else {
                    StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY
                }
            },
        }
    }

    /// Message safe to expose to API callers. Internal-class errors are
    /// replaced with a generic phrase; validation/auth-style messages are
    /// authored to be safe and are passed through.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn public_message(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Validation { message, .. } => message.clone(),
            Self::NotFound { resource, lookup } => {
                format!("{resource} not found (lookup: {lookup})")
            },
            Self::Unauthorized(m) => format!("unauthenticated: {m}"),
            Self::Forbidden(m) => format!("forbidden: {m}"),
            Self::Conflict(m) => format!("conflict: {m}"),
            Self::RateLimited(m) => format!("rate limit exceeded: {m}"),
            Self::Timeout(_) => "the operation timed out; it may be retried".to_owned(),
            Self::Cancelled(_) => "the operation was cancelled".to_owned(),
            Self::ExternalService { service, .. } => {
                format!("upstream dependency '{service}' is temporarily unavailable")
            },
            Self::Database(_) | Self::Messaging(_) | Self::Serialization(_) | Self::Internal(_) => {
                "an internal error occurred".to_owned()
            },
            Self::ExternalFailure { message, .. } => message.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Field-level issues for `Validation` errors; empty otherwise.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn validation_issues(&self) -> &[ValidationIssue] {
        match self {
            Self::Validation { issues, .. } => issues,
            _ => &[],
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Conversions from common third-party error types.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

impl From<uuid::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: uuid::Error) -> Self {
        Self::invalid_field("id", "invalid_format", format!("invalid UUID: {err}"))
    }
}

impl From<serde_json::Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: serde_json::Error) -> Self {
        Self::Serialization(err.to_string())
    }
}

impl From<url::ParseError> for AppError {
    fn from(err: url::ParseError) -> Self {
        Self::invalid_field("url", "invalid_format", format!("invalid URL: {err}"))
    }
}

impl From<chrono::ParseError> for AppError {
    fn from(err: chrono::ParseError) -> Self {
        Self::invalid_field(
            "timestamp",
            "invalid_format",
            format!("invalid timestamp: {err}"),
        )
    }
}

impl From<base64::DecodeError> for AppError {
    fn from(err: base64::DecodeError) -> Self {
        Self::validation(format!("invalid base64 payload: {err}"))
    }
}

impl From<std::num::ParseIntError> for AppError {
    fn from(err: std::num::ParseIntError) -> Self {
        Self::validation(format!("invalid integer: {err}"))
    }
}

impl From<std::num::TryFromIntError> for AppError {
    fn from(err: std::num::TryFromIntError) -> Self {
        Self::validation(format!("integer out of range: {err}"))
    }
}

impl From<std::string::FromUtf8Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: std::string::FromUtf8Error) -> Self {
        Self::Serialization(format!("invalid UTF-8: {err}"))
    }
}

impl From<std::str::Utf8Error> for AppError {
    fn from(err: std::str::Utf8Error) -> Self {
        Self::Serialization(format!("invalid UTF-8: {err}"))
    }
}
```

```rust
//! PURPOSE:
//! The `Execution` aggregate: one complete workflow/agent run, and the only
//! place allowed to change an execution's status.
//!
//! This file is the durability anchor of the whole pipeline. Every status the
//! platform ever reports for an execution originates from a transition applied
//! here, which means every status carries an actor, a timestamp, a version and
//! (on failure) a classified reason.
//!
//! Layer / ownership
//! -----------------
//! `mas-domain`. Pure: no database, no broker, no transport. The application
//! layer orchestrates persistence around the transitions this aggregate
//! performs; the worker and the orchestration engine perform them too, but
//! only through these methods.
//!
//! Production responsibility
//! -------------------------
//! * Enforce the canonical execution state machine (see
//!   [`crate::state_machine::ExecutionStateMachine`]). Illegal moves fail with
//!   `Conflict` — they never coerce and never silently no-op.
//! * Make cancellation durable and idempotent: requesting it is a flag that
//!   can be set repeatedly; applying it is a terminal transition that refuses
//!   to reopen a completed or already-cancelled execution.
//! * Keep a monotonic `version` so a stale worker — one that lost ownership —
//!   cannot overwrite a newer state. The version bumps on **every** applied
//!   transition, including the cancellation flag.
//!
//! What this module must NOT do
//! ----------------------------
//! * It must NOT persist anything, publish events, or talk to a clock service.
//! * It must NOT add lifecycle states beyond the ones the domain requires.
//! * It must NOT store secrets: `failure` is a truncated, already-redacted
//!   summary produced by callers.
//!
//! Child executions (agent delegation) form a tree via
//! `parent_execution_id` / `root_execution_id`; the root is its own root.

use mas_common::constants;
use mas_common::enums::ExecutionStatus;
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{
    AgentId, ExecutionId, OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId, WorkflowId, WorkflowVersionId,
};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_common::validation;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::state_machine::{
    illegal_transition, terminal_conflict, AggregateKind, CancellationOutcome, CancellationSignal,
    ExecutionStateMachine, StateTransition, TransitionActor, TransitionFailure, TransitionLog,
};

/// Accumulated resource consumption of an execution.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ResourceUsageSummary {
    pub steps_executed: u32,
    pub tool_calls: u32,
    pub tokens_input: u64,
    pub tokens_output: u64,
    /// Wall-clock runtime accumulated while running (ms; excludes pauses).
    pub active_time_ms: u64,
}

impl ResourceUsageSummary {
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn total_tokens(&self) -> u64 {
        self.tokens_input + self.tokens_output
    }
}

/// Serde default for the version column: versions are 1-based, and rows
/// written before versioning existed must hydrate as version 1 rather than 0.
const fn default_version() -> u64 {
    1
}

/// The execution aggregate.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Execution {
    pub id: ExecutionId,
    pub tenant_id: TenantId,
    pub organization_id: OrganizationId,
    pub project_id: ProjectId,
    /// Definition source: a published workflow version…
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub workflow_id: Option<WorkflowId>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub workflow_version_id: Option<WorkflowVersionId>,
    /// …or an agent.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub agent_id: Option<AgentId>,
    /// Delegation tree.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub parent_execution_id: Option<ExecutionId>,
    pub root_execution_id: ExecutionId,
    /// End-to-end tracing key supplied at intake.
    pub correlation_id: String,
    pub status: ExecutionStatus,
    /// Coordinated stop flag: the runtime checks this and transitions to
    /// `Cancelled` at the next safe point.
    cancellation_requested: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub input: serde_json::Value,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub output: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub failure: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub started_at: Option<Timestamp>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub finished_at: Option<Timestamp>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub deadline: Option<Timestamp>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub resource_usage: ResourceUsageSummary,
    pub created_by: String,
    pub created_at: Timestamp,
    pub updated_at: Timestamp,
    /// Monotonic version, bumped by every applied transition. It is the
    /// fence a stale worker trips over: a write carrying an older version is
    /// rejected rather than clobbering newer state.
    #[serde(default = "default_version")]
    pub version: u64,
    /// Transitions applied since the last drain. Diagnostics and outbox
    /// source only — never persisted with the aggregate.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing)]
    transitions: TransitionLog,
}

impl Execution {
    /// Creates a root execution in `Pending`.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        tenant_id: TenantId,
        organization_id: OrganizationId,
        project_id: ProjectId,
        workflow_id: Option<WorkflowId>,
        agent_id: Option<AgentId>,
        input: serde_json::Value,
        correlation_id: impl Into<String>,
        created_by: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let correlation_id = correlation_id.into();
        let created_by = created_by.into();
        validation::validate_non_empty("correlation_id", &correlation_id)?;
        validation::validate_length("correlation_id", &correlation_id, 1, 256)?;
        validation::validate_non_empty("created_by", &created_by)?;
        if workflow_id.is_none() && agent_id.is_none() {
            return Err(AppError::invalid_field(
                "execution",
                "missing_target",
                "execution requires a workflow or agent target",
            ));
        }
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        let id = ExecutionId::new();
        Ok(Self {
            id,
            tenant_id,
            organization_id,
            project_id,
            workflow_id,
            workflow_version_id: None,
            agent_id,
            parent_execution_id: None,
            root_execution_id: id, // root is its own root
            correlation_id,
            status: ExecutionStatus::Pending,
            cancellation_requested: false,
            input,
            output: None,
            failure: None,
            started_at: None,
            finished_at: None,
            deadline: None,
            resource_usage: ResourceUsageSummary::default(),
            created_by,
            created_at: now,
            updated_at: now,
            version: 1,
            transitions: TransitionLog::new(),
        })
    }

    /// Derives a child execution (agent delegation). Links into the same
    /// correlation tree and enforces depth/size limits indirectly via IDs.
    pub fn spawn_child(&self, agent_id: AgentId, input: serde_json::Value) -> Result<Self> {
        if self.status.is_terminal() {
            return Err(AppError::conflict(format!(
                "execution {} in status '{}' cannot delegate",
                self.id, self.status
            )));
        }
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        Ok(Self {
            id: ExecutionId::new(),
            tenant_id: self.tenant_id,
            organization_id: self.organization_id,
            project_id: self.project_id,
            workflow_id: None,
            workflow_version_id: None,
            agent_id: Some(agent_id),
            parent_execution_id: Some(self.id),
            root_execution_id: self.root_execution_id,
            correlation_id: self.correlation_id.clone(),
            status: ExecutionStatus::Pending,
            cancellation_requested: false,
            input,
            output: None,
            failure: None,
            started_at: None,
            finished_at: None,
            deadline: self.deadline, // children never outlive the parent's deadline
            resource_usage: ResourceUsageSummary::default(),
            created_by: format!("execution:{}", self.id),
            created_at: now,
            updated_at: now,
            version: 1,
            transitions: TransitionLog::new(),
        })
    }

    /// `true` when this execution started the tree (no parent).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_root(&self) -> bool {
        self.id == self.root_execution_id
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub const fn cancellation_requested(&self) -> bool {
        self.cancellation_requested
    }

    /// The monotonic version (1-based; every applied transition bumps it).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn version(&self) -> u64 {
        self.version
    }

    /// Transitions recorded since the last drain (diagnostics only).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn transitions(&self) -> &TransitionLog {
        &self.transitions
    }

    /// Removes and returns the recorded transitions, for the caller to persist
    /// as audit + outbox rows.
    pub fn take_transitions(&mut self) -> Vec<StateTransition> {
        self.transitions.drain()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_expired(&self) -> bool {
        self.deadline.is_some_and(|deadline| !deadline.is_future())
    }

    pub fn set_deadline(&mut self, deadline: Timestamp) -> Result<()> {
        if !deadline.is_future() {
            return Err(AppError::invalid_field(
                "deadline",
                "out_of_range",
                "deadline must be in the future",
            ));
        }
        self.deadline = Some(deadline);
        self.touch();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Runtime accounting hook (adds to the running totals, enforcing hard caps).
    pub fn record_usage(&mut self, usage: ResourceUsageSummary) -> Result<()> {
        let next_steps = self
            .resource_usage
            .steps_executed
            .saturating_add(usage.steps_executed);
        let next_tools = self
            .resource_usage
            .tool_calls
            .saturating_add(usage.tool_calls);
        if next_steps > constants::MAX_STEPS_PER_EXECUTION {
            return Err(AppError::rate_limited(
                "execution exceeded maximum step count",
            ));
        }
        if next_tools > constants::MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_EXECUTION {
            return Err(AppError::rate_limited(
                "execution exceeded maximum tool calls",
            ));
        }
        self.resource_usage.steps_executed = next_steps;
        self.resource_usage.tool_calls = next_tools;
        self.resource_usage.tokens_input = self
            .resource_usage
            .tokens_input
            .saturating_add(usage.tokens_input);
        self.resource_usage.tokens_output = self
            .resource_usage
            .tokens_output
            .saturating_add(usage.tokens_output);
        self.resource_usage.active_time_ms = self
            .resource_usage
            .active_time_ms
            .saturating_add(usage.active_time_ms);
        self.touch();
        Ok(())
    }

    // -- lifecycle -----------------------------------------------------------

    /// Pending → Queued: the execution is durable, committed and visible to
    /// the dispatcher, but no runner owns it yet.
    pub fn enqueue(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        self.apply(ExecutionStatus::Queued, actor, None, "enqueue")
    }

    /// Pending|Queued → Running.
    pub fn start(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        if self.is_expired() {
            return Err(AppError::timeout("execution deadline passed before start"));
        }
        let transition = self.apply(ExecutionStatus::Running, actor, None, "start")?;
        self.started_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Running → Paused.
    pub fn pause(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        self.apply(ExecutionStatus::Paused, actor, None, "pause")
    }

    /// Paused → Running.
    pub fn resume(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        if self.is_expired() {
            return Err(AppError::timeout("execution deadline passed while paused"));
        }
        self.apply(ExecutionStatus::Running, actor, None, "resume")
    }

    /// Sets the cooperative cancellation flag.
    ///
    /// Idempotent: a second request returns `already_requested = true` and
    /// does **not** bump the version or raise — repeated operator or API calls
    /// must not turn into spurious conflicts. A terminal execution cannot be
    /// flagged at all: there is nothing left to stop.
    pub fn request_cancellation(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<CancellationSignal> {
        if self.status.is_terminal() {
            return Err(terminal_conflict(
                AggregateKind::Execution,
                &self.id.to_string(),
                "request_cancellation",
                self.status.as_str(),
            ));
        }
        let already_requested = self.cancellation_requested;
        if !already_requested {
            self.cancellation_requested = true;
            self.version = self.version.saturating_add(1);
        }
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        self.updated_at = now;
        Ok(CancellationSignal {
            aggregate: AggregateKind::Execution,
            aggregate_id: self.id.to_string(),
            actor: actor.clone(),
            requested_at: now,
            version: self.version,
            already_requested,
        })
    }

    /// Immediate transition to `Cancelled` (the runtime honored the flag, or
    /// an operator forced it). Terminal and idempotent.
    ///
    /// A completed or failed execution is **never** reopened: the request is
    /// rejected rather than being turned into a late cancellation that would
    /// erase a real outcome.
    pub fn cancel(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<CancellationOutcome> {
        if self.status == ExecutionStatus::Cancelled {
            return Ok(CancellationOutcome::AlreadyCancelled);
        }
        let transition = self.apply(ExecutionStatus::Cancelled, actor, None, "cancel")?;
        self.cancellation_requested = true;
        self.finished_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        Ok(CancellationOutcome::Cancelled(transition))
    }

    /// Running|Paused → Completed (terminal). Output must be a JSON value
    /// already validated by the execution layer.
    ///
    /// A cancellation request is honoured over completion: an execution that
    /// was asked to stop must end as cancelled, never as completed.
    pub fn complete(
        &mut self,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        output: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        if self.cancellation_requested {
            return Err(AppError::conflict(
                "cancellation was requested; execution must end as cancelled",
            ));
        }
        let transition = self.apply(ExecutionStatus::Completed, actor, None, "complete")?;
        self.output = output;
        self.finished_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Running|Paused → Failed (terminal), carrying a classified failure.
    ///
    /// The failure is *classified*, not merely described: the retry decision
    /// downstream keys off `failure.retryable`, never off prose matching.
    pub fn fail(
        &mut self,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        failure: TransitionFailure,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        let mut message = failure.message.clone();
        message.truncate(4096);
        self.failure = Some(message);
        let transition = self.apply(ExecutionStatus::Failed, actor, Some(failure), "fail")?;
        self.finished_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Wall time since start (None if never started).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn elapsed(&self) -> Option<Duration> {
        let started = self.started_at?;
        let end = self.finished_at.unwrap_or_else(Timestamp::now);
        end.duration_since(&started)
    }

    // -- the single transition gate -----------------------------------------

    /// Applies one canonical transition: validates it against the state
    /// machine, mutates the status, bumps the version, and records the
    /// transition. Every public status change funnels through here, so no
    /// caller can bypass validation by editing `status` some other way.
    fn apply(
        &mut self,
        to: ExecutionStatus,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        failure: Option<TransitionFailure>,
        action: &str,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        let from = self.status;
        if !ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(from, to) {
            let error = if from.is_terminal() {
                terminal_conflict(
                    AggregateKind::Execution,
                    &self.id.to_string(),
                    action,
                    from.as_str(),
                )
            } else {
                illegal_transition(
                    AggregateKind::Execution,
                    &self.id.to_string(),
                    action,
                    from.as_str(),
                    to.as_str(),
                )
            };
            return Err(error);
        }
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        self.status = to;
        self.version = self.version.saturating_add(1);
        self.updated_at = now;
        let transition = StateTransition {
            aggregate: AggregateKind::Execution,
            aggregate_id: self.id.to_string(),
            from: from.as_str().to_owned(),
            to: to.as_str().to_owned(),
            actor: actor.clone(),
            occurred_at: now,
            version: self.version,
            failure,
            correlation_id: Some(self.correlation_id.clone()),
        };
        self.transitions.record(transition.clone());
        Ok(transition)
    }

    fn touch(&mut self) {
        self.updated_at = Timestamp::now();
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::state_machine::ActorKind;

    fn actor() -> TransitionActor {
        TransitionActor::worker("w-1").expect("actor")
    }

    fn execution() -> Execution {
        Execution::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            OrganizationId::new(),
            ProjectId::new(),
            Some(WorkflowId::new()),
            None,
            serde_json::json!({"n": 1}),
            "corr-1",
            "user-1",
        )
        .expect("execution")
    }

    fn failure() -> TransitionFailure {
        TransitionFailure::terminal("agent_unavailable", "no route to host").expect("failure")
    }

    #[test]
    fn new_executions_start_pending_at_version_one() {
        let execution = execution();
        assert_eq!(execution.status, ExecutionStatus::Pending);
        assert_eq!(execution.version(), 1);
        assert!(execution.transitions().is_empty());
        assert!(execution.is_root());
    }

    #[test]
    fn happy_path_records_every_transition_with_actor_and_version() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        let queued = execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        assert_eq!(queued.from, "pending");
        assert_eq!(queued.to, "queued");
        assert_eq!(queued.version, 2);
        assert_eq!(queued.actor.kind, ActorKind::Worker);

        let running = execution.start(&actor()).expect("start");
        assert_eq!(running.to, "running");
        assert_eq!(running.version, 3);
        assert!(execution.started_at.is_some());

        let completed = execution
            .complete(&actor(), Some(serde_json::json!({"ok": true})))
            .expect("complete");
        assert_eq!(completed.to, "completed");
        assert_eq!(completed.version, 4);
        assert!(execution.finished_at.is_some());
        assert_eq!(execution.output, Some(serde_json::json!({"ok": true})));

        let log = execution.take_transitions();
        assert_eq!(log.len(), 3);
        assert!(execution.transitions().is_empty(), "drain is destructive");
    }

    #[test]
    fn illegal_transitions_fail_safely_and_change_nothing() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        let version_before = execution.version();
        let error = execution
            .complete(&actor(), None)
            .expect_err("pending cannot complete");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert_eq!(execution.status, ExecutionStatus::Pending);
        assert_eq!(
            execution.version(),
            version_before,
            "a rejected transition must not bump the version"
        );
        assert!(execution.transitions().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn terminal_executions_are_never_reopened() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        execution.start(&actor()).expect("start");
        execution.complete(&actor(), None).expect("complete");

        for (label, result) in [
            ("start", execution.start(&actor()).map(|_| ())),
            ("pause", execution.pause(&actor()).map(|_| ())),
            ("enqueue", execution.enqueue(&actor()).map(|_| ())),
            ("fail", execution.fail(&actor(), failure()).map(|_| ())),
        ] {
            let error = result.expect_err(label);
            assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)), "{label}: {error:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(execution.status, ExecutionStatus::Completed);

        // Cancelling a completed execution is refused, not silently applied.
        assert!(execution.cancel(&actor()).is_err());
        assert_eq!(execution.status, ExecutionStatus::Completed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancellation_is_idempotent_and_never_reopens() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        execution.start(&actor()).expect("start");

        let first = execution
            .request_cancellation(&actor())
            .expect("first request");
        assert!(!first.already_requested);
        let version_after_first = execution.version();

        let second = execution
            .request_cancellation(&actor())
            .expect("second request is a no-op, not an error");
        assert!(second.already_requested);
        assert_eq!(
            execution.version(),
            version_after_first,
            "a repeated signal must not bump the version"
        );

        assert!(matches!(
            execution.cancel(&actor()).expect("cancel"),
            CancellationOutcome::Cancelled(_)
        ));
        assert_eq!(execution.status, ExecutionStatus::Cancelled);
        assert!(matches!(
            execution.cancel(&actor()).expect("repeat cancel"),
            CancellationOutcome::AlreadyCancelled
        ));

        // A terminal execution cannot even be flagged.
        assert!(execution.request_cancellation(&actor()).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancellation_requested_blocks_completion() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        execution.start(&actor()).expect("start");
        execution.request_cancellation(&actor()).expect("flag");

        let error = execution
            .complete(&actor(), None)
            .expect_err("a cancelled run must not complete");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert_eq!(execution.status, ExecutionStatus::Running);
    }

    #[test]
    fn failure_transitions_carry_classified_information() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        execution.start(&actor()).expect("start");
        let transition = execution
            .fail(
                &actor(),
                TransitionFailure::transient("rate_limited", "429").expect("f"),
            )
            .expect("fail");
        assert_eq!(transition.to, "failed");
        assert!(transition.is_failure());
        assert!(transition.is_retryable());
        assert_eq!(
            transition.failure.as_ref().map(|f| f.code.clone()),
            Some("rate_limited".to_owned())
        );
        assert!(execution.failure.is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn pause_resume_round_trip() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        execution.start(&actor()).expect("start");
        assert_eq!(execution.pause(&actor()).expect("pause").to, "paused");
        assert_eq!(execution.resume(&actor()).expect("resume").to, "running");
        assert!(
            execution.pause(&actor()).is_ok() && execution.pause(&actor()).is_err(),
            "pausing twice is illegal"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn paused_executions_may_still_fail() {
        let mut execution = execution();
        execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        execution.start(&actor()).expect("start");
        execution.pause(&actor()).expect("pause");
        assert_eq!(
            execution.fail(&actor(), failure()).expect("fail").to,
            "failed"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn transitions_are_not_serialized_into_the_aggregate() {
        // Encoded before any local binding can shadow the `execution()` fixture.
        let mut legacy_json = serde_json::to_value(execution()).expect("a fresh execution encodes");
        legacy_json
            .as_object_mut()
            .expect("object")
            .remove("version");

        let mut execution = execution();
        execution.enqueue(&actor()).expect("enqueue");
        let encoded = serde_json::to_value(&execution).expect("encode");
        assert!(
            encoded.get("transitions").is_none(),
            "the transition log is an in-memory drain queue, never persisted state"
        );
        assert_eq!(encoded.get("version").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()), Some(2));

        // A row written before versioning existed hydrates at version 1, not 0:
        // a zero version would make every compare-and-swap fence meaningless.
        let legacy: Execution =
            serde_json::from_value(legacy_json).expect("a pre-versioning row must still hydrate");
        assert_eq!(legacy.version(), 1);
        assert!(legacy.transitions().is_empty());
    }
}
```
