```rust
//! PURPOSE:
//! The durable idempotency contract for execution submission.
//!
//! This module owns the *decision* — given the record a key collision found,
//! is this submission new, a safe replay, or a deterministic conflict? It does
//! not own the storage (that is a persistence concern) and it does not own the
//! hashing (that lives one layer up, in `mas-application`, because it needs a
//! digest implementation and this crate stays dependency-light).
//!
//! Layer / ownership
//! -----------------
//! `mas-domain`. Pure data + pure decision logic. The Postgres implementation
//! and the in-memory reference implementation of the durable port both call
//! [`IdempotencyRecord::decide`], so the three outcomes cannot drift between
//! them.
//!
//! Production responsibility
//! -------------------------
//! * Make duplicate submission **safe**: the same key with the same request
//!   fingerprint returns the original execution instead of running paid AI
//!   work twice.
//! * Make conflicting submission **deterministic**: the same key with a
//!   *different* fingerprint is a hard conflict, never a silent overwrite and
//!   never a silent replay of someone else's request.
//! * Keep the fingerprint **secret-free**: only a digest is ever stored, so
//!   the ledger cannot leak request bodies.
//!
//! What this module must NOT do
//! ----------------------------
//! * It must NOT perform a SELECT-then-INSERT. The caller inserts with a
//!   database-enforced unique constraint and only then consults this module to
//!   classify the outcome.
//! * It must NOT store raw request payloads, secrets or credentials.
//! * It must NOT decide *how long* keys are retained — retention is an
//!   operational concern of the persistence layer.

use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{ExecutionId, TaskId, TenantId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_common::validation;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Maximum accepted length of a client-supplied idempotency key.
///
/// Deliberately reuses the platform constant so a key accepted by the API can
/// always be stored by the ledger.
pub const MAX_KEY_LENGTH: usize = mas_common::constants::MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_LENGTH;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The record
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// One row of the idempotency ledger.
///
/// Only digests are stored. `fingerprint` identifies *what* was requested and
/// `response_digest` identifies *what* was returned, so a replay can be proven
/// to be the same answer rather than merely "an answer".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct IdempotencyRecord {
    /// Owning tenant — the uniqueness scope is (tenant, key).
    pub tenant_id: TenantId,
    /// Client-supplied duplicate-submission guard.
    pub idempotency_key: String,
    /// Hex digest of the canonical request. Never the request itself.
    pub fingerprint: String,
    /// Digest of the response returned for the original submission.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub response_digest: Option<String>,
    /// Execution the original submission created.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub execution_id: Option<ExecutionId>,
    /// Task the original submission created.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub task_id: Option<TaskId>,
    /// When the original submission committed.
    pub created_at: Timestamp,
    /// Last time the record was read or written.
    pub updated_at: Timestamp,
}

impl IdempotencyRecord {
    /// Builds a record, validating the key and the digest shape.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        tenant_id: TenantId,
        idempotency_key: impl Into<String>,
        fingerprint: impl Into<String>,
        response_digest: Option<String>,
        execution_id: Option<ExecutionId>,
        task_id: Option<TaskId>,
        now: &Timestamp,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let idempotency_key = idempotency_key.into();
        let fingerprint = fingerprint.into();
        validation::validate_non_empty("idempotency_key", &idempotency_key)?;
        validation::validate_length("idempotency_key", &idempotency_key, 1, MAX_KEY_LENGTH)?;
        Self::validate_fingerprint(&fingerprint)?;
        if let Some(digest) = response_digest.as_deref() {
            Self::validate_fingerprint(digest)?;
        }
        if execution_id.is_none() && task_id.is_none() {
            return Err(AppError::invalid_field(
                "idempotency_record",
                "missing_target",
                "an idempotency record must reference the execution or task it guards",
            ));
        }
        Ok(Self {
            tenant_id,
            idempotency_key,
            fingerprint,
            response_digest,
            execution_id,
            task_id,
            created_at: *now,
            updated_at: *now,
        })
    }

    /// Whether a fingerprint is structurally a plausible digest.
    ///
    /// The ledger must never store raw request bodies, so a value that is not
    /// a bounded hex token is rejected rather than persisted.
    pub fn validate_fingerprint(fingerprint: &str) -> Result<()> {
        validation::validate_non_empty("fingerprint", fingerprint)?;
        validation::validate_length("fingerprint", fingerprint, 1, 128)?;
        if !fingerprint.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
            return Err(AppError::invalid_field(
                "fingerprint",
                "not_a_digest",
                "fingerprints must be hex digests; raw request data is never stored",
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Classification of a key collision.
    ///
    /// The three outcomes are exhaustive and mutually exclusive:
    ///
    /// * [`IdempotencyDecision::New`] — no record; the caller may proceed.
    /// * [`IdempotencyDecision::Replay`] — same key, same fingerprint: return
    ///   the original result, run nothing.
    /// * [`IdempotencyDecision::Conflict`] — same key, different fingerprint:
    ///   the client reused a key for a different request. This is a client
    ///   error and must surface as `409 Conflict`, never as a silent replay.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn decide(existing: Option<&IdempotencyRecord>, fingerprint: &str) -> IdempotencyDecision {
        match existing {
            None => IdempotencyDecision::New,
            Some(record) if record.fingerprint == fingerprint => IdempotencyDecision::Replay {
                record: record.clone(),
            },
            Some(record) => IdempotencyDecision::Conflict {
                record: record.clone(),
            },
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The decision
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Outcome of presenting an idempotency key + fingerprint to the ledger.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum IdempotencyDecision {
    /// Nothing stored under this key — proceed with submission.
    New,
    /// Same key, same request: replay the recorded result.
    Replay {
        /// The stored record.
        record: IdempotencyRecord,
    },
    /// Same key, different request: a deterministic conflict.
    Conflict {
        /// The stored record (its fingerprint differs from the presented one).
        record: IdempotencyRecord,
    },
}

impl IdempotencyDecision {
    /// `true` when the caller may create new durable work.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_new(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::New)
    }

    /// `true` when the caller must return the previously recorded result.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_replay(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Replay { .. })
    }

    /// `true` when the caller must reject the submission.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_conflict(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Conflict { .. })
    }

    /// A stable token for metrics and logs.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn metric_token(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::New => "new",
            Self::Replay { .. } => "replay",
            Self::Conflict { .. } => "conflict",
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn now() -> Timestamp {
        Timestamp::from_unix_seconds(1_700_000_000).expect("timestamp")
    }

    fn record(key: &str, fingerprint: &str) -> IdempotencyRecord {
        IdempotencyRecord::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            key,
            fingerprint,
            None,
            Some(ExecutionId::new()),
            Some(TaskId::new()),
            &now(),
        )
        .expect("record")
    }

    const DIGEST_A: &str = "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa";
    const DIGEST_B: &str = "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb";

    #[test]
    fn no_record_means_new() {
        let decision = IdempotencyRecord::decide(None, DIGEST_A);
        assert!(decision.is_new());
        assert_eq!(decision.metric_token(), "new");
    }

    #[test]
    fn same_key_same_fingerprint_is_a_safe_replay() {
        let stored = record("k", DIGEST_A);
        let decision = IdempotencyRecord::decide(Some(&stored), DIGEST_A);
        assert!(decision.is_replay());
        assert!(!decision.is_new());
        assert_eq!(decision.metric_token(), "replay");
        match decision {
            IdempotencyDecision::Replay { record } => {
                assert_eq!(record.execution_id, stored.execution_id);
            },
            other => panic!("expected replay, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn same_key_different_fingerprint_is_a_deterministic_conflict() {
        let stored = record("k", DIGEST_A);
        let decision = IdempotencyRecord::decide(Some(&stored), DIGEST_B);
        assert!(decision.is_conflict());
        assert!(
            !decision.is_replay(),
            "a conflicting request must never replay"
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.metric_token(), "conflict");
        match decision {
            IdempotencyDecision::Conflict { record } => {
                assert_eq!(record.fingerprint, DIGEST_A);
            },
            other => panic!("expected conflict, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn records_reject_raw_request_data_instead_of_a_digest() {
        let error = IdempotencyRecord::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            "k",
            "{\"prompt\":\"secret\"}",
            None,
            Some(ExecutionId::new()),
            None,
            &now(),
        )
        .expect_err("raw JSON must not be storable as a fingerprint");
        assert!(
            matches!(error, AppError::Validation { .. }),
            "got {error:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn records_require_a_target_and_a_non_empty_key() {
        assert!(IdempotencyRecord::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            "",
            DIGEST_A,
            None,
            Some(ExecutionId::new()),
            None,
            &now(),
        )
        .is_err());
        assert!(
            IdempotencyRecord::new(TenantId::new(), "k", DIGEST_A, None, None, None, &now(),)
                .is_err()
        );
        assert!(IdempotencyRecord::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            "k",
            DIGEST_A,
            None,
            None,
            Some(TaskId::new()),
            &now(),
        )
        .is_ok());
        assert!(IdempotencyRecord::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            "x".repeat(MAX_KEY_LENGTH + 1),
            DIGEST_A,
            None,
            Some(ExecutionId::new()),
            None,
            &now(),
        )
        .is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn response_digest_is_validated_when_present() {
        assert!(IdempotencyRecord::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            "k",
            DIGEST_A,
            Some("not-hex".to_owned()),
            Some(ExecutionId::new()),
            None,
            &now(),
        )
        .is_err());
        assert!(IdempotencyRecord::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            "k",
            DIGEST_A,
            Some(DIGEST_B.to_owned()),
            Some(ExecutionId::new()),
            None,
            &now(),
        )
        .is_ok());
    }
}

//! PURPOSE: The pure domain model: aggregates, their lifecycle invariants and
//! shared value objects.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-domain`.
//!
//! Production responsibility: make illegal states unrepresentable — every
//! transition is a method that validates before it applies, records who did it
//! and when, and bumps the aggregate's version so a stale writer can be
//! detected downstream.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • depend on HTTP, SQL, messaging or any infrastructure crate — this crate
//!     depends only on `mas-common` and pure data libraries;
//!   • perform I/O of any kind;
//!   • expose a setter that changes state without going through a transition.

//! # mas-domain
//!
//! Pure domain model of the platform: aggregates, their lifecycle invariants
//! and shared value objects.
//!
//! Dependency rule (enforced by manifest): this crate depends only on
//! `mas-common` and pure data libraries. It contains **no** HTTP/database/
//! messaging/LLM logic; behavior beyond validation/state transitions lives in
//! the application and orchestration layers.

pub mod agent;
pub mod agent_capability;
pub mod agent_version;

pub mod credential;

// already owns that name (a usage actor is a different concept from a

```rust
//! PURPOSE:
//! The **single canonical state machine** for the durable execution pipeline.
//!
//! This module owns the one definition of "what may become what" for the
//! execution, task and task-attempt aggregates, and it owns the one shape of
//! the record a transition leaves behind. It exists because the platform
//! previously grew several ad-hoc lifecycle lanes (an orchestration engine
//! lane, a worker lane, a service lane) that each invented their own idea of a
//! legal move; this module is the authority they must all defer to.
//!
//! Layer / ownership
//! -----------------
//! `mas-domain` owns this file. It is pure: no database, no broker, no clock
//! beyond the [`Timestamp`] value it is handed, no I/O of any kind. The
//! application, worker and persistence layers *call* it; they never
//! re-implement it.
//!
//! Production responsibility
//! -------------------------
//! * Every durable state change — and only a durable state change — produces a
//!   [`StateTransition`] carrying source state, target state, acting actor,
//!   occurrence timestamp, the post-transition version, and the classified
//!   failure information when the move was a failure.
//! * Illegal transitions **fail safely**: they return an
//!   [`AppError::Conflict`] naming the aggregate, the action and the current
//!   state. They never silently coerce, never skip a state, and never
//!   resurrect a terminal aggregate.
//! * Versioning is monotonic and owned here: each applied transition bumps the
//!   aggregate version by exactly one, which is what makes stale-worker writes
//!   detectable downstream.
//!
//! What this module must NOT do
//! ----------------------------
//! * It must NOT acquire locks, write to a database or publish events. It
//!   decides *whether* a move is legal and *what record* it leaves; someone
//!   else persists that decision.
//! * It must NOT invent new lifecycle states. The state sets are the ones the
//!   domain already requires; adding a state here without a domain need is a
//!   defect, not a feature.
//! * It must NOT hold secrets. Failure messages are truncated, caller-supplied
//!   and already-redacted summaries; this module never sees a credential.

use mas_common::enums::{ExecutionStatus, TaskStatus};
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::TenantId;
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_common::validation;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Bounds
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Hard cap on a stable failure code (machine-readable, short).
pub const MAX_FAILURE_CODE_LENGTH: usize = 128;
/// Hard cap on a human-readable failure message (safe summaries only).
pub const MAX_FAILURE_MESSAGE_LENGTH: usize = 2048;
/// Hard cap on an actor identifier.
pub const MAX_ACTOR_ID_LENGTH: usize = 128;
/// Transitions retained per aggregate before the oldest are dropped. The log
/// is a diagnostic + outbox source, not an audit store: the authoritative
/// history is the `audit_events` table.
pub const MAX_RECORDED_TRANSITIONS: usize = 64;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Aggregate & actor identity
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Which durable aggregate a transition belongs to.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AggregateKind {
    /// One complete workflow/agent run.
    Execution,
    /// One unit of dispatched work.
    Task,
    /// One execution try of a task.
    TaskAttempt,
}

impl AggregateKind {
    /// Canonical wire/database token.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Execution => "execution",
            Self::Task => "task",
            Self::TaskAttempt => "task_attempt",
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for AggregateKind {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.as_str())
    }
}

/// Who (or what) caused a transition. Recorded so an operator can tell a user
/// cancellation from a worker crash-recovery move without guesswork.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ActorKind {
    /// An authenticated human principal (user or API key acting for one).
    Principal,
    /// A worker process performing durable queue work.
    Worker,
    /// An internal platform service (scheduler, recovery sweep, relay).
    System,
    /// The outbox relay, when a transition is a consequence of publication.
    Relay,
}

impl ActorKind {
    /// Canonical wire/database token.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Principal => "principal",
            Self::Worker => "worker",
            Self::System => "system",
            Self::Relay => "relay",
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ActorKind {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.as_str())
    }
}

/// The acting identity behind one transition.
///
/// The identifier is a stable, non-secret label: a principal id, a worker name,
/// or a service name. It is deliberately *not* a credential, a token or an
/// email address, because transitions are logged.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TransitionActor {
    /// Class of actor.
    pub kind: ActorKind,
    /// Stable identifier within that class.
    pub id: String,
    /// Tenant the actor was scoped to, when the actor is tenant-scoped.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub tenant_id: Option<TenantId>,
}

impl TransitionActor {
    /// A tenant-scoped human/API-key principal.
    pub fn principal(id: impl Into<String>, tenant_id: TenantId) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            kind: ActorKind::Principal,
            id: Self::checked_id(id)?,
            tenant_id: Some(tenant_id),
        })
    }

    /// A worker process. Workers are not tenant-scoped: one worker drains rows
    /// for many tenants, and the row — not the worker — carries the tenancy.
    pub fn worker(id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            kind: ActorKind::Worker,
            id: Self::checked_id(id)?,
            tenant_id: None,
        })
    }

    /// An internal platform service.
    pub fn system(id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            kind: ActorKind::System,
            id: Self::checked_id(id)?,
            tenant_id: None,
        })
    }

    /// The outbox relay.
    pub fn relay(id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            kind: ActorKind::Relay,
            id: Self::checked_id(id)?,
            tenant_id: None,
        })
    }

    /// Attaches a tenant scope (used when a system actor adopts a tenant for
    /// the duration of one unit of work, e.g. a scheduler tick).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_tenant(mut self, tenant_id: TenantId) -> Self {
        self.tenant_id = Some(tenant_id);
        self
    }

    /// `worker:w-1` — the form used in log lines and audit detail.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn label(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}:{}", self.kind, self.id)
    }

    fn checked_id(id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<String> {
        let id = id.into();
        validation::validate_non_empty("actor.id", &id)?;
        validation::validate_length("actor.id", &id, 1, MAX_ACTOR_ID_LENGTH)?;
        Ok(id)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Failure classification carried by a transition
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The classified failure behind a transition into `Failed` (or the terminal
/// outcome of a task attempt).
///
/// `code` is a stable, machine-readable token — never a free-form sentence —
/// so retry logic, dashboards and alert routing can key off it. `message` is a
/// safe, already-redacted summary intended for humans.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TransitionFailure {
    /// Stable machine-readable error code.
    pub code: String,
    /// Safe human-readable summary (redacted upstream, truncated here).
    pub message: String,
    /// Whether retrying the unit of work could plausibly succeed.
    pub retryable: bool,
}

impl TransitionFailure {
    /// Builds a failure, validating and truncating both fields.
    pub fn new(
        code: impl Into<String>,
        message: impl Into<String>,
        retryable: bool,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut code = code.into();
        let mut message = message.into();
        validation::validate_non_empty("failure.code", &code)?;
        code.truncate(MAX_FAILURE_CODE_LENGTH);
        message.truncate(MAX_FAILURE_MESSAGE_LENGTH);
        Ok(Self {
            code,
            message,
            retryable,
        })
    }

    /// A failure that retrying cannot fix (authn/authz, malformed input, …).
    pub fn terminal(code: impl Into<String>, message: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::new(code, message, false)
    }

    /// A failure a later attempt may plausibly clear (broker, rate limit, …).
    pub fn transient(code: impl Into<String>, message: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::new(code, message, true)
    }

    /// Canonical wire token for the retry class.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn class(&self) -> &'static str {
        if self.retryable {
            "transient"
        } else {
            "terminal"
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The transition record
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// One durable state change, fully described.
///
/// Every field here exists because an operator or a downstream consumer needs
/// it: `from`/`to` to reconstruct the timeline, `actor` to attribute the move,
/// `occurred_at` to order it, `version` to fence stale writers, and `failure`
/// to classify the reason without parsing prose.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StateTransition {
    /// Aggregate the transition applied to.
    pub aggregate: AggregateKind,
    /// Aggregate identifier (as a string so the record stays transport-agnostic).
    pub aggregate_id: String,
    /// State before the transition.
    pub from: String,
    /// State after the transition.
    pub to: String,
    /// Who caused it.
    pub actor: TransitionActor,
    /// When it happened.
    pub occurred_at: Timestamp,
    /// Aggregate version *after* the transition was applied (1-based).
    pub version: u64,
    /// Classified failure, when the transition was a failure.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub failure: Option<TransitionFailure>,
    /// End-to-end correlation key, when the caller had one.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub correlation_id: Option<String>,
}

impl StateTransition {
    /// `true` when the transition moved the aggregate into a failure state.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_failure(&self) -> bool {
        self.failure.is_some()
    }

    /// `true` when a retry could plausibly succeed.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
        self.failure
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|failure| failure.retryable)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Transition log (in-aggregate, drained by the persistence layer)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Bounded, append-only log of the transitions an aggregate has taken.
///
/// It exists so the application layer can hand the audit sink and the outbox
/// exactly the transitions a unit of work produced, without re-deriving them
/// from a before/after diff. Bounded because it lives in memory on the
/// aggregate: the authoritative history is the audit ledger.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TransitionLog {
    entries: Vec<StateTransition>,
}

impl TransitionLog {
    /// An empty log.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Appends a transition, dropping the oldest when the bound is reached.
    pub fn record(&mut self, transition: StateTransition) {
        if self.entries.len() >= MAX_RECORDED_TRANSITIONS {
            self.entries.remove(0);
        }
        self.entries.push(transition);
    }

    /// Removes and returns every recorded transition (drain-then-persist).
    pub fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<StateTransition> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.entries)
    }

    /// Borrows the recorded transitions.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn entries(&self) -> &[StateTransition] {
        &self.entries
    }

    /// The most recent transition, if any.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn last(&self) -> Option<&StateTransition> {
        self.entries.last()
    }

    /// Number of retained transitions.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.len()
    }

    /// Whether nothing has been recorded.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.entries.is_empty()
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Execution state machine
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The canonical execution lifecycle.
///
/// ```text
///   pending ──► queued ──► running ──► completed   (terminal)
///      │           │          │  ╲
///      │           │          │   ╲──► failed      (terminal)
///      │           │          │
///      │           │          ├────► paused ──► running
///      │           │          │
///      └───────────┴──────────┴────► cancelled    (terminal)
/// ```
///
/// `paused` is kept because the runtime genuinely suspends runs awaiting
/// approval; removing it would delete working behavior, and the domain still
/// requires it. No other state may be added without a domain need.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ExecutionStateMachine;

impl ExecutionStateMachine {
    /// Whether `from → to` is a legal execution transition.
    ///
    /// Self-transitions are `false` except for the idempotent
    /// `cancelled → cancelled` case, which the aggregate handles before
    /// consulting this table (a repeated cancellation is a no-op, not an
    /// error).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn can_transition(from: ExecutionStatus, to: ExecutionStatus) -> bool {
        use ExecutionStatus as S;
        match (from, to) {
            // Intake: created, then made visible to the dispatcher.
            (S::Pending, S::Queued) => true,
            // A pending execution may also be started directly (the durable
            // task is created and claimed in the same breath) or cancelled
            // before it ever reaches a worker.
            (S::Pending, S::Running) => true,
            (S::Pending, S::Cancelled) => true,
            (S::Pending, S::Failed) => true,
            // Dispatch: a worker claimed the durable task.
            (S::Queued, S::Running) => true,
            (S::Queued, S::Cancelled) => true,
            (S::Queued, S::Failed) => true,
            // Running may complete, fail, be cancelled, or pause for approval.
            (S::Running, S::Completed) => true,
            (S::Running, S::Failed) => true,
            (S::Running, S::Cancelled) => true,
            (S::Running, S::Paused) => true,
            // Paused resumes, or ends.
            (S::Paused, S::Running) => true,
            (S::Paused, S::Completed) => true,
            (S::Paused, S::Failed) => true,
            (S::Paused, S::Cancelled) => true,
            // Everything else — including every move out of a terminal state —
            // is illegal.
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// The legal targets of `from`, in declaration order.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn legal_targets(from: ExecutionStatus) -> Vec<ExecutionStatus> {
        ExecutionStatus::ALL
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|to| Self::can_transition(from, *to))
            .collect()
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Task state machine
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The canonical task lifecycle.
///
/// ```text
///   pending ──► queued ──► running ──► completed   (terminal)
///      │           │          │
///      │           │          ├──────► failed ──► queued     (retry)
///      │           │          │                  ╲
///      │           │          │                   ╲──► dead_lettered (terminal)
///      │           │          │
///      └───────────┴──────────┴──────────────────► cancelled (terminal)
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TaskStateMachine;

impl TaskStateMachine {
    /// Whether `from → to` is a legal task transition.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn can_transition(from: TaskStatus, to: TaskStatus) -> bool {
        use TaskStatus as S;
        match (from, to) {
            // Intake: created, then made claimable.
            (S::Pending, S::Queued) => true,
            (S::Pending, S::Cancelled) => true,
            (S::Pending, S::Failed) => true,
            // Claim: exactly one worker moves the row to running.
            (S::Queued, S::Running) => true,
            (S::Queued, S::Cancelled) => true,
            (S::Queued, S::Failed) => true,
            // Settlement.
            (S::Running, S::Completed) => true,
            (S::Running, S::Failed) => true,
            (S::Running, S::Cancelled) => true,
            // Retry or dead-letter after a failure.
            (S::Failed, S::Queued) => true,
            (S::Failed, S::DeadLettered) => true,
            // Everything else is illegal: a terminal task is never reopened.
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// The legal targets of `from`, in declaration order.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn legal_targets(from: TaskStatus) -> Vec<TaskStatus> {
        TaskStatus::ALL
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|to| Self::can_transition(from, *to))
            .collect()
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Shared guard helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Renders the "illegal transition" error every aggregate raises.
///
/// Centralised so the message shape is identical across aggregates: an
/// operator grepping for one phrasing finds every rejection.
#[must_use]
pub fn illegal_transition(
    aggregate: AggregateKind,
    aggregate_id: &str,
    action: &str,
    from: &str,
    to: &str,
) -> AppError {
    AppError::conflict(format!(
        "illegal {aggregate} transition: cannot {action} {aggregate_id} from '{from}' to '{to}'"
    ))
}

/// Renders the "already terminal, refusing to reopen" error.
#[must_use]
pub fn terminal_conflict(
    aggregate: AggregateKind,
    aggregate_id: &str,
    action: &str,
    status: &str,
) -> AppError {
    AppError::conflict(format!(
        "{aggregate} {aggregate_id} is already terminal in state '{status}'; refusing to {action}"
    ))
}

/// A cooperative cancellation signal that did **not** change the aggregate's
/// status (the run is still finishing a safe point).
///
/// Returned by cancellation requests so the caller can persist the flag and
/// emit a signal event without pretending the status moved. `already_requested`
/// makes the operation idempotent: a second request is a no-op, not a conflict.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CancellationSignal {
    /// Aggregate the signal applies to.
    pub aggregate: AggregateKind,
    /// Aggregate identifier.
    pub aggregate_id: String,
    /// Who requested it.
    pub actor: TransitionActor,
    /// When this request was recorded.
    pub requested_at: Timestamp,
    /// Aggregate version after the flag was set.
    pub version: u64,
    /// `true` when the flag was already set (idempotent no-op).
    pub already_requested: bool,
}

/// Result of asking an aggregate to cancel: either a real terminal transition,
/// or an acknowledgement that it was already cancelled.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CancellationOutcome {
    /// The aggregate moved into `cancelled`.
    Cancelled(StateTransition),
    /// It was already cancelled; nothing changed.
    AlreadyCancelled,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use mas_common::ids::TenantId;

    fn actor() -> TransitionActor {
        TransitionActor::worker("w-1").expect("worker actor")
    }

    #[test]
    fn actor_ids_are_validated() {
        assert!(TransitionActor::worker("").is_err());
        assert!(TransitionActor::worker("x".repeat(MAX_ACTOR_ID_LENGTH + 1)).is_err());
        assert!(TransitionActor::worker("w-1").is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn actor_label_is_stable_and_secret_free() {
        let worker = TransitionActor::worker("w-7").expect("actor");
        assert_eq!(worker.label(), "worker:w-7");
        let tenant = TenantId::new();
        let principal = TransitionActor::principal("user-9", tenant).expect("actor");
        assert_eq!(principal.label(), "principal:user-9");
        assert_eq!(principal.tenant_id, Some(tenant));
    }

    #[test]
    fn failure_fields_are_truncated_and_classified() {
        let failure =
            TransitionFailure::terminal("x".repeat(500), "y".repeat(9_000)).expect("failure");
        assert_eq!(failure.code.len(), MAX_FAILURE_CODE_LENGTH);
        assert_eq!(failure.message.len(), MAX_FAILURE_MESSAGE_LENGTH);
        assert_eq!(failure.class(), "terminal");
        assert!(!failure.retryable);

        let transient =
            TransitionFailure::transient("upstream_unavailable", "try again").expect("failure");
        assert_eq!(transient.class(), "transient");
        assert!(transient.retryable);
        assert!(TransitionFailure::new("", "m", true).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn execution_forbids_reopening_terminal_states() {
        for terminal in [
            ExecutionStatus::Completed,
            ExecutionStatus::Failed,
            ExecutionStatus::Cancelled,
        ] {
            for target in ExecutionStatus::ALL {
                assert!(
                    !ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(terminal, *target),
                    "{terminal} must not transition to {target}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn execution_happy_path_and_pause_are_legal() {
        assert!(ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Pending,
            ExecutionStatus::Queued
        ));
        assert!(ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Queued,
            ExecutionStatus::Running
        ));
        assert!(ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Running,
            ExecutionStatus::Paused
        ));
        assert!(ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Paused,
            ExecutionStatus::Running
        ));
        assert!(ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Running,
            ExecutionStatus::Completed
        ));
        assert!(ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Running,
            ExecutionStatus::Failed
        ));
        assert!(ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Running,
            ExecutionStatus::Cancelled
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn execution_forbids_nonsense_moves() {
        assert!(!ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Pending,
            ExecutionStatus::Completed
        ));
        assert!(!ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Pending,
            ExecutionStatus::Paused
        ));
        assert!(!ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Queued,
            ExecutionStatus::Completed
        ));
        assert!(!ExecutionStateMachine::can_transition(
            ExecutionStatus::Running,
            ExecutionStatus::Queued
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn task_forbids_reopening_terminal_states() {
        for terminal in [
            TaskStatus::Completed,
            TaskStatus::Cancelled,
            TaskStatus::DeadLettered,
        ] {
            for target in TaskStatus::ALL {
                assert!(
                    !TaskStateMachine::can_transition(terminal, *target),
                    "{terminal} must not transition to {target}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn task_retry_and_dead_letter_are_legal_only_from_failed() {
        assert!(TaskStateMachine::can_transition(
            TaskStatus::Failed,
            TaskStatus::Queued
        ));
        assert!(TaskStateMachine::can_transition(
            TaskStatus::Failed,
            TaskStatus::DeadLettered
        ));
        assert!(!TaskStateMachine::can_transition(
            TaskStatus::Running,
            TaskStatus::Queued
        ));
        assert!(!TaskStateMachine::can_transition(
            TaskStatus::Pending,
            TaskStatus::DeadLettered
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn legal_targets_match_the_table() {
        let targets = ExecutionStateMachine::legal_targets(ExecutionStatus::Running);
        assert_eq!(
            targets,
            vec![
                ExecutionStatus::Paused,
                ExecutionStatus::Completed,
                ExecutionStatus::Failed,
                ExecutionStatus::Cancelled,
            ]
        );
        let task_targets = TaskStateMachine::legal_targets(TaskStatus::Queued);
        assert_eq!(
            task_targets,
            vec![
                TaskStatus::Running,
                TaskStatus::Failed,
                TaskStatus::Cancelled
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn transition_log_bounded_and_drainable() {
        let mut log = TransitionLog::new();
        for index in 0..(MAX_RECORDED_TRANSITIONS + 10) {
            log.record(StateTransition {
                aggregate: AggregateKind::Task,
                aggregate_id: format!("task-{index}"),
                from: "queued".to_owned(),
                to: "running".to_owned(),
                actor: actor(),
                occurred_at: Timestamp::now(),
                version: u64::try_from(index).expect("fits") + 1,
                failure: None,
                correlation_id: None,
            });
        }
        assert_eq!(log.len(), MAX_RECORDED_TRANSITIONS);
        let first = log.entries().first().expect("first");
        assert_eq!(
            first.aggregate_id, "task-10",
            "oldest entries dropped first"
        );
        assert_eq!(log.drain().len(), MAX_RECORDED_TRANSITIONS);
        assert!(log.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn transition_records_expose_failure_semantics() {
        let failed = StateTransition {
            aggregate: AggregateKind::Execution,
            aggregate_id: "exec-1".to_owned(),
            from: "running".to_owned(),
            to: "failed".to_owned(),
            actor: actor(),
            occurred_at: Timestamp::now(),
            version: 3,
            failure: Some(TransitionFailure::transient("rate_limited", "slow down").expect("f")),
            correlation_id: Some("corr-1".to_owned()),
        };
        assert!(failed.is_failure());
        assert!(failed.is_retryable());

        let completed = StateTransition {
            failure: None,
            to: "completed".to_owned(),
            ..failed.clone()
        };
        assert!(!completed.is_failure());
        assert!(!completed.is_retryable());
    }

    #[test]
    fn illegal_transition_errors_name_every_part() {
        let error = illegal_transition(
            AggregateKind::Task,
            "task-42",
            "complete",
            "queued",
            "completed",
        );
        let rendered = format!("{error}");
        assert!(rendered.contains("task"), "names the aggregate: {rendered}");
        assert!(rendered.contains("task-42"), "names the id: {rendered}");
        assert!(
            rendered.contains("complete"),
            "names the action: {rendered}"
        );
        assert!(rendered.contains("queued"), "names the source: {rendered}");
        assert!(
            rendered.contains("completed"),
            "names the target: {rendered}"
        );
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));

        let terminal = terminal_conflict(AggregateKind::Execution, "exec-9", "start", "completed");
        assert!(matches!(terminal, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert!(format!("{terminal}").contains("already terminal"));
    }
}

_PURPOSE ব্লক এই ফাইলের হেডারে নেই; ফাইলটি জেনারেটেড বা কনফিগারেশন-মাত্র._

```rust
//! PURPOSE:
//! The `Task` aggregate: one unit of dispatched durable work, and the only
//! place allowed to change a task's status or ownership.
//!
//! A task is what a worker actually claims. It must therefore contain
//! *everything* needed to recover it after a restart: the execution it
//! belongs to, its tenant/project scope, the target runtime, the attempt
//! counts, the ownership fence, and every lifecycle timestamp. If any of
//! those lived only in memory or only in a broker frame, a process restart
//! would silently lose it.
//!
//! Layer / ownership
//! -----------------
//! `mas-domain`. Pure. Persistence, claiming and dispatch live in
//! `mas-persistence` / `mas-worker` and drive this aggregate's methods.
//!
//! Production responsibility
//! -------------------------
//! * Enforce the canonical task state machine (see
//!   [`crate::state_machine::TaskStateMachine`]).
//! * Own the **ownership fence**: `locked_by` + `locked_until` + `version`
//!   together let a repository reject a write from a worker that no longer
//!   owns the task. A stale worker must never transition a task it lost.
//! * Derive attempt budget from durable state (`attempt_count` /
//!   `max_attempts`), never from broker delivery metadata. The broker is a
//!   wake-up hint; it is not an authority on how many times work ran.
//!
//! What this module must NOT do
//! ----------------------------
//! * It must NOT persist anything or talk to infrastructure.
//! * It must NOT keep a second, parallel notion of task state. There is one
//!   status field and one state machine.
//! * It must NOT store secrets in `last_error`; it is a redacted summary.

use mas_common::enums::{TaskPriority, TaskStatus};
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{
    AgentId, ExecutionId, OrganizationId, ProjectId, TaskAttemptId, TaskId, TenantId, WorkflowId,
};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_common::validation;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::state_machine::{
    illegal_transition, terminal_conflict, AggregateKind, CancellationOutcome, StateTransition,
    TaskStateMachine, TransitionActor, TransitionFailure, TransitionLog,
};

/// Serde default for the version column (versions are 1-based).
const fn default_version() -> u64 {
    1
}

/// The task aggregate.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Task {
    pub id: TaskId,
    pub tenant_id: TenantId,
    pub organization_id: OrganizationId,
    pub project_id: ProjectId,
    /// Exactly one of `agent_id` / `workflow_id` addresses the target runtime.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub agent_id: Option<AgentId>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub workflow_id: Option<WorkflowId>,
    /// Owning execution, when the task was spawned by one.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub execution_id: Option<ExecutionId>,
    /// The requested operation (e.g. `agent.run`, `tool.invoke`, `workflow.step`).
    pub operation: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub input: serde_json::Value,
    pub priority: TaskPriority,
    pub status: TaskStatus,
    /// Client-supplied duplicate-submission guard (unique per tenant).
    pub idempotency_key: String,
    /// Earliest time the task may be claimed (retry backoff).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub not_before: Option<Timestamp>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub deadline: Option<Timestamp>,
    pub max_attempts: u32,
    pub attempt_count: u32,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub queued_at: Option<Timestamp>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub started_at: Option<Timestamp>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub finished_at: Option<Timestamp>,
    /// Safe (redacted, truncated) description of the last failure.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub last_error: Option<String>,
    /// Stable machine-readable code for the last failure (retry decisions key
    /// off this, never off prose).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub last_error_code: Option<String>,
    /// Worker identity currently owning the task (`None` when unclaimed).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub locked_by: Option<String>,
    /// When the current ownership expires (lease/heartbeat window).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub locked_until: Option<Timestamp>,
    /// The attempt row this ownership belongs to.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub last_attempt_id: Option<TaskAttemptId>,
    pub created_by: String,
    pub created_at: Timestamp,
    pub updated_at: Timestamp,
    /// Monotonic version, bumped by every applied transition.
    #[serde(default = "default_version")]
    pub version: u64,
    /// Transitions applied since the last drain (never persisted).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing)]
    transitions: TransitionLog,
}

impl Task {
    /// Creates a task in `Pending` (not yet queued).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        tenant_id: TenantId,
        organization_id: OrganizationId,
        project_id: ProjectId,
        agent_id: Option<AgentId>,
        workflow_id: Option<WorkflowId>,
        operation: impl Into<String>,
        input: serde_json::Value,
        priority: TaskPriority,
        idempotency_key: impl Into<String>,
        created_by: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let operation = operation.into();
        let idempotency_key = idempotency_key.into();
        let created_by = created_by.into();
        validation::validate_non_empty("operation", &operation)?;
        validation::validate_length("operation", &operation, 1, 128)?;
        validation::validate_non_empty("idempotency_key", &idempotency_key)?;
        validation::validate_length(
            "idempotency_key",
            &idempotency_key,
            1,
            mas_common::constants::MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_LENGTH,
        )?;
        validation::validate_non_empty("created_by", &created_by)?;
        if agent_id.is_none() && workflow_id.is_none() {
            return Err(AppError::invalid_field(
                "task",
                "missing_target",
                "task must target an agent or a workflow",
            ));
        }
        if agent_id.is_some() && workflow_id.is_some() {
            return Err(AppError::invalid_field(
                "task",
                "ambiguous_target",
                "task targets either an agent or a workflow, never both",
            ));
        }
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        Ok(Self {
            id: TaskId::new(),
            tenant_id,
            organization_id,
            project_id,
            agent_id,
            workflow_id,
            execution_id: None,
            operation,
            input,
            priority,
            status: TaskStatus::Pending,
            idempotency_key,
            not_before: None,
            deadline: None,
            max_attempts: mas_common::constants::DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES + 1,
            attempt_count: 0,
            queued_at: None,
            started_at: None,
            finished_at: None,
            last_error: None,
            last_error_code: None,
            locked_by: None,
            locked_until: None,
            last_attempt_id: None,
            created_by,
            created_at: now,
            updated_at: now,
            version: 1,
            transitions: TransitionLog::new(),
        })
    }

    /// Links the task to the execution it serves.
    ///
    /// Called during atomic submission: the execution and its first task are
    /// created together, so the link is set before either is visible.
    pub fn attach_execution(&mut self, execution_id: ExecutionId) -> Result<()> {
        if self.execution_id.is_some() && self.execution_id != Some(execution_id) {
            return Err(AppError::conflict(format!(
                "task {} already belongs to another execution",
                self.id
            )));
        }
        self.execution_id = Some(execution_id);
        self.touch();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Whether the task blew its deadline.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_expired(&self) -> bool {
        self.deadline.is_some_and(|deadline| !deadline.is_future())
    }

    /// Remaining attempts (excluding the current one).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn remaining_attempts(&self) -> u32 {
        self.max_attempts.saturating_sub(self.attempt_count)
    }

    /// Whether another attempt is permitted by the durable budget.
    ///
    /// Deliberately derived from `attempt_count`, which is bumped only by a
    /// real start transition — never from a broker redelivery counter.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn has_attempts_remaining(&self) -> bool {
        self.attempt_count < self.max_attempts
    }

    /// The monotonic version (1-based).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn version(&self) -> u64 {
        self.version
    }

    /// Transitions recorded since the last drain.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn transitions(&self) -> &TransitionLog {
        &self.transitions
    }

    /// Removes and returns the recorded transitions for persistence.
    pub fn take_transitions(&mut self) -> Vec<StateTransition> {
        self.transitions.drain()
    }

    /// Earliest time the task may be claimed.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn available_at(&self) -> Timestamp {
        self.not_before.unwrap_or(self.created_at)
    }

    /// Whether the task is currently claimable: queued, not before its
    /// availability time, and not holding a live ownership fence.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_claimable_at(&self, now: &Timestamp) -> bool {
        if self.status != TaskStatus::Queued {
            return false;
        }
        if self.available_at().is_after(now) {
            return false;
        }
        !self.is_owned_at(now)
    }

    /// Whether a live ownership fence exists at `now`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_owned_at(&self, now: &Timestamp) -> bool {
        match (self.locked_by.as_deref(), self.locked_until) {
            (Some(_), None) => true,
            (Some(_), Some(until)) => until.is_after(now),
            (None, _) => false,
        }
    }

    /// Whether `worker` currently owns this task at `now`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_owned_by_at(&self, worker: &str, now: &Timestamp) -> bool {
        self.locked_by.as_deref() == Some(worker) && self.is_owned_at(now)
    }

    /// Installs an ownership fence. Only a claim (or a renew) may do this; it
    /// is the durable half of "exactly one worker runs this task".
    pub fn assign_ownership(
        &mut self,
        worker: &str,
        until: Timestamp,
        attempt_id: TaskAttemptId,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        if worker.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(AppError::invalid_field(
                "locked_by",
                "empty",
                "ownership requires a worker identity",
            ));
        }
        self.locked_by = Some(worker.to_owned());
        self.locked_until = Some(until);
        self.last_attempt_id = Some(attempt_id);
        self.touch();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Extends an existing fence. Refuses to steal: only the current owner may
    /// renew, so a second worker cannot silently take over a live task.
    pub fn renew_ownership(&mut self, worker: &str, until: Timestamp) -> Result<()> {
        match self.locked_by.as_deref() {
            Some(owner) if owner == worker => {
                self.locked_until = Some(until);
                self.touch();
                Ok(())
            },
            Some(_) | None => Err(AppError::conflict(format!(
                "worker '{worker}' cannot renew ownership of task {}; it does not own it",
                self.id
            ))),
        }
    }

    /// Clears the fence (settlement, or an expired lease being reclaimed).
    pub fn release_ownership(&mut self) {
        self.locked_by = None;
        self.locked_until = None;
        self.touch();
    }

    // -- state transitions ---------------------------------------------------

    /// Pending → Queued.
    pub fn queue(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        if self.is_expired() {
            return Err(AppError::validation("task deadline has already passed"));
        }
        let transition = self.apply(TaskStatus::Queued, actor, None, "queue")?;
        self.queued_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Queued → Running for `worker`, consuming one attempt and installing
    /// the ownership fence in the same move.
    ///
    /// Ownership and the status change are one operation on purpose: a task
    /// that is `running` but unowned is unreclaimable after a crash, and a
    /// task that is owned but `queued` can be double-claimed.
    pub fn start(
        &mut self,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        worker: &str,
        lease_until: Timestamp,
        attempt_id: TaskAttemptId,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        if self.is_expired() {
            return Err(AppError::timeout("task deadline has passed before start"));
        }
        if !self.has_attempts_remaining() {
            return Err(AppError::conflict(format!(
                "task {} has exhausted its {} attempts",
                self.id, self.max_attempts
            )));
        }
        let transition = self.apply(TaskStatus::Running, actor, None, "start")?;
        self.attempt_count = self.attempt_count.saturating_add(1);
        self.started_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        self.finished_at = None;
        self.assign_ownership(worker, lease_until, attempt_id)?;
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Running → Completed (terminal), clearing the fence.
    pub fn complete(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        let transition = self.apply(TaskStatus::Completed, actor, None, "complete")?;
        self.finished_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        self.last_error = None;
        self.last_error_code = None;
        self.release_ownership();
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Running → Failed with a classified failure.
    pub fn fail(
        &mut self,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        failure: TransitionFailure,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        let mut message = failure.message.clone();
        message.truncate(2048);
        self.last_error = Some(message);
        self.last_error_code = Some(failure.code.clone());
        let transition = self.apply(TaskStatus::Failed, actor, Some(failure), "fail")?;
        self.finished_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        self.release_ownership();
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Failed → Queued after `delay`, when attempts remain. Use
    /// [`Task::dead_letter`] otherwise.
    pub fn retry(
        &mut self,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        delay: std::time::Duration,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        // Retrying is only meaningful after a failure. Guarding it explicitly
        // keeps `pending → queued` (the normal queueing move) from being
        // reachable under the name "retry", which would let a caller re-queue
        // work that has never run.
        if self.status != TaskStatus::Failed {
            return Err(illegal_transition(
                AggregateKind::Task,
                &self.id.to_string(),
                "retry",
                self.status.as_str(),
                TaskStatus::Queued.as_str(),
            ));
        }
        if !self.has_attempts_remaining() {
            return Err(AppError::conflict(
                "task has no remaining attempts; dead-letter it instead",
            ));
        }
        let transition = self.apply(TaskStatus::Queued, actor, None, "retry")?;
        let now = transition.occurred_at;
        self.queued_at = Some(now);
        self.started_at = None;
        self.finished_at = None;
        self.not_before = now.checked_add(delay);
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Failed → DeadLettered (terminal).
    pub fn dead_letter(
        &mut self,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        reason: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        let mut reason = reason.into();
        reason.truncate(2048);
        let transition = self.apply(TaskStatus::DeadLettered, actor, None, "dead-letter")?;
        self.last_error = Some(format!("dead-lettered: {reason}"));
        self.release_ownership();
        Ok(transition)
    }

    /// Pending|Queued|Running → Cancelled (terminal, idempotent).
    ///
    /// A completed, failed or dead-lettered task is never reopened: cancelling
    /// one is refused rather than erasing a real outcome.
    pub fn cancel(&mut self, actor: &TransitionActor) -> Result<CancellationOutcome> {
        if self.status == TaskStatus::Cancelled {
            return Ok(CancellationOutcome::AlreadyCancelled);
        }
        let transition = self.apply(TaskStatus::Cancelled, actor, None, "cancel")?;
        self.finished_at = Some(transition.occurred_at);
        self.release_ownership();
        Ok(CancellationOutcome::Cancelled(transition))
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_terminal(&self) -> bool {
        self.status.is_terminal()
    }

    // -- the single transition gate -----------------------------------------

    /// Applies one canonical task transition. Every public status change
    /// funnels through here so validation cannot be bypassed.
    fn apply(
        &mut self,
        to: TaskStatus,
        actor: &TransitionActor,
        failure: Option<TransitionFailure>,
        action: &str,
    ) -> Result<StateTransition> {
        let from = self.status;
        if !TaskStateMachine::can_transition(from, to) {
            let error = if from.is_terminal() {
                terminal_conflict(
                    AggregateKind::Task,
                    &self.id.to_string(),
                    action,
                    from.as_str(),
                )
            } else {
                illegal_transition(
                    AggregateKind::Task,
                    &self.id.to_string(),
                    action,
                    from.as_str(),
                    to.as_str(),
                )
            };
            return Err(error);
        }
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        self.status = to;
        self.version = self.version.saturating_add(1);
        self.updated_at = now;
        let transition = StateTransition {
            aggregate: AggregateKind::Task,
            aggregate_id: self.id.to_string(),
            from: from.as_str().to_owned(),
            to: to.as_str().to_owned(),
            actor: actor.clone(),
            occurred_at: now,
            version: self.version,
            failure,
            correlation_id: None,
        };
        self.transitions.record(transition.clone());
        Ok(transition)
    }

    fn touch(&mut self) {
        self.updated_at = Timestamp::now();
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use mas_common::ids::WorkflowId;

    fn actor() -> TransitionActor {
        TransitionActor::worker("w-1").expect("actor")
    }

    fn task() -> Task {
        Task::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            OrganizationId::new(),
            ProjectId::new(),
            None,
            Some(WorkflowId::new()),
            "execution.run",
            serde_json::json!({}),
            TaskPriority::High,
            "idem-1",
            "svc-test",
        )
        .expect("task")
    }

    fn failure(retryable: bool) -> TransitionFailure {
        TransitionFailure::new("upstream_unavailable", "bus is down", retryable).expect("failure")
    }

    fn future(secs: u64) -> Timestamp {
        Timestamp::now()
            .checked_add(std::time::Duration::from_secs(secs))
            .expect("timestamp")
    }

    #[test]
    fn new_tasks_are_pending_unowned_and_unreclaimed() {
        let task = task();
        assert_eq!(task.status, TaskStatus::Pending);
        assert_eq!(task.version(), 1);
        assert!(task.locked_by.is_none());
        assert_eq!(task.attempt_count, 0);
        assert!(task.has_attempts_remaining());
        assert!(
            !task.is_claimable_at(&Timestamp::now()),
            "pending is not claimable"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn queue_then_claim_installs_the_ownership_fence() {
        let mut task = task();
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        assert!(task.is_claimable_at(&now));

        let attempt = TaskAttemptId::new();
        let lease = future(30);
        let started = task.start(&actor(), "w-1", lease, attempt).expect("start");
        assert_eq!(started.to, "running");
        assert_eq!(task.attempt_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(task.locked_by.as_deref(), Some("w-1"));
        assert_eq!(task.last_attempt_id, Some(attempt));
        assert!(task.is_owned_by_at("w-1", &now));
        assert!(!task.is_owned_by_at("w-2", &now));
        assert!(
            !task.is_claimable_at(&now),
            "an owned task must never be claimable"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn ownership_renewal_refuses_to_steal() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("start");

        assert!(task.renew_ownership("w-1", future(60)).is_ok());
        let error = task
            .renew_ownership("w-2", future(60))
            .expect_err("another worker must not renew someone else's lease");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert_eq!(task.locked_by.as_deref(), Some("w-1"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn expired_leases_are_claimable_again() {
        let now = Timestamp::now();
        let mut task = task();
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-1", now, TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("start");
        assert!(
            !task.is_owned_at(&now),
            "a lease that expires exactly now has lapsed: it must be renewed before expiry"
        );
        let earlier = Timestamp::from_unix_ms(now.to_unix_ms() - 1).expect("timestamp");
        assert!(
            task.is_owned_at(&earlier),
            "a lease is live until its expiry"
        );
        assert!(
            !task.is_owned_at(&future(1)),
            "an expired lease frees the task"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn attempt_budget_comes_from_durable_state_not_the_broker() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.max_attempts = 2;
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("attempt 1");

        task.fail(&actor(), failure(true)).expect("fail");
        assert!(task.has_attempts_remaining());
        task.retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
            .expect("retry");
        assert!(task.not_before.is_some(), "retry schedules a backoff");
        assert!(task.started_at.is_none());

        task.start(&actor(), "w-2", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("attempt 2");
        assert_eq!(task.attempt_count, 2);
        assert!(!task.has_attempts_remaining());

        task.fail(&actor(), failure(true)).expect("fail");
        let error = task
            .retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::ZERO)
            .expect_err("no attempts left");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert!(
            task.dead_letter(&actor(), "attempts exhausted").is_ok(),
            "exhausted tasks go to the dead-letter queue"
        );
        assert_eq!(task.status, TaskStatus::DeadLettered);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_zero_attempt_budget_refuses_to_start_at_all() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.max_attempts = 0;
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");

        let version_before = task.version();
        let error = task
            .start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect_err("no attempt budget");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert_eq!(task.status, TaskStatus::Queued);
        assert_eq!(task.attempt_count, 0, "a refused start consumes no attempt");
        assert_eq!(task.version(), version_before);
        assert!(
            task.locked_by.is_none(),
            "a refused start installs no fence"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn retrying_is_only_legal_after_a_failure() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        let error = task
            .retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::ZERO)
            .expect_err("a queued task has nothing to retry");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert_eq!(task.status, TaskStatus::Queued);

        task.start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("start");
        let error = task
            .retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::ZERO)
            .expect_err("a running task has nothing to retry");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn exhausting_the_budget_dead_letters_instead_of_looping() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.max_attempts = 2;
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("attempt 1");
        task.fail(&actor(), failure(true)).expect("fail");
        task.retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::ZERO)
            .expect("retry after attempt 1");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-2", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("attempt 2");
        task.fail(&actor(), failure(true)).expect("fail");

        assert_eq!(task.attempt_count, 2);
        assert!(
            task.retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::ZERO).is_err(),
            "no retries remain"
        );
        assert!(task.dead_letter(&actor(), "attempts exhausted").is_ok());
        assert_eq!(task.status, TaskStatus::DeadLettered);
    }

    #[test]
    fn settlement_clears_the_fence_and_records_the_failure_class() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("start");
        let transition = task.fail(&actor(), failure(true)).expect("fail");
        assert!(transition.is_retryable());
        assert_eq!(
            task.last_error_code.as_deref(),
            Some("upstream_unavailable")
        );
        assert!(task.locked_by.is_none(), "failure releases the fence");

        task.retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::ZERO)
            .expect("retry");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-2", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("start");
        let completed = task.complete(&actor()).expect("complete");
        assert_eq!(completed.to, "completed");
        assert!(task.last_error.is_none(), "success clears the last error");
        assert!(task.locked_by.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancel_is_idempotent_and_never_reopens_a_finished_task() {
        let mut cancelled_task = task();
        cancelled_task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        assert!(matches!(
            cancelled_task.cancel(&actor()).expect("first cancel"),
            CancellationOutcome::Cancelled(_)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            cancelled_task.cancel(&actor()).expect("second cancel"),
            CancellationOutcome::AlreadyCancelled
        ));

        let mut completed_task = task();
        completed_task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        completed_task
            .start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("start");
        completed_task.complete(&actor()).expect("complete");
        let error = completed_task
            .cancel(&actor())
            .expect_err("a completed task must not be cancelled");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Conflict(_)));
        assert_eq!(completed_task.status, TaskStatus::Completed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn illegal_moves_fail_safely_and_leave_state_untouched() {
        let mut task = task();
        let version_before = task.version();
        assert!(matches!(
            task.complete(&actor())
                .expect_err("pending cannot complete"),
            AppError::Conflict(_)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            task.retry(&actor(), std::time::Duration::ZERO)
                .expect_err("pending cannot retry"),
            AppError::Conflict(_)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            task.dead_letter(&actor(), "nope")
                .expect_err("pending cannot dead-letter"),
            AppError::Conflict(_)
        ));
        assert_eq!(task.status, TaskStatus::Pending);
        assert_eq!(task.version(), version_before);
        assert!(task.transitions().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn transitions_are_recorded_and_drainable() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        task.start(&actor(), "w-1", future(30), TaskAttemptId::new())
            .expect("start");
        task.complete(&actor()).expect("complete");
        let log = task.take_transitions();
        assert_eq!(log.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(log.first().map(|t| t.to.clone()), Some("queued".to_owned()));
        assert_eq!(
            log.last().map(|t| t.to.clone()),
            Some("completed".to_owned())
        );
        assert!(task.transitions().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn transitions_are_never_persisted_with_the_aggregate() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.queue(&actor()).expect("queue");
        let encoded = serde_json::to_value(&task).expect("encode");
        assert!(encoded.get("transitions").is_none());
        assert_eq!(encoded.get("version").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()), Some(2));
    }

    #[test]
    fn expired_deadlines_block_queue_and_start() {
        let mut task = task();
        task.deadline = Some(Timestamp::from_unix_ms(1).expect("past"));
        assert!(task.is_expired());
        assert!(
            task.queue(&actor()).is_err(),
            "an expired task cannot be queued"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn execution_attachment_is_once_only() {
        let mut task = task();
        let execution = ExecutionId::new();
        task.attach_execution(execution).expect("attach");
        task.attach_execution(execution)
            .expect("reattaching the same execution is a no-op");
        assert!(
            task.attach_execution(ExecutionId::new()).is_err(),
            "a task cannot be re-parented"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn targets_are_exactly_one_of_agent_or_workflow() {
        let base = || {
            (
                TenantId::new(),
                OrganizationId::new(),
                ProjectId::new(),
                TaskPriority::Normal,
            )
        };
        let (t, o, p, pr) = base();
        assert!(Task::new(
            t,
            o,
            p,
            None,
            None,
            "execution.run",
            serde_json::json!({}),
            pr,
            "k",
            "u"
        )
        .is_err());
        let (t, o, p, pr) = base();
        assert!(Task::new(
            t,
            o,
            p,
            Some(AgentId::new()),
            Some(WorkflowId::new()),
            "execution.run",
            serde_json::json!({}),
            pr,
            "k",
            "u"
        )
        .is_err());
        let (t, o, p, pr) = base();
        assert!(Task::new(
            t,
            o,
            p,
            Some(AgentId::new()),
            None,
            "execution.run",
            serde_json::json!({}),
            pr,
            "k",
            "u"
        )
        .is_ok());
    }
}
