### FILE: `enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/persistence/tests/tenant_sql_contract.rs`

**PURPOSE:**

```text
The database-level half of the multi-tenant isolation guarantee:
a static contract test over the SQL the durable pipeline actually issues.

Owning layer: `mas-persistence` (the production repositories).

Production responsibility: behavioural tests prove that tenant B is refused
*today*. They cannot prove that the next statement someone adds is scoped.
This file closes that gap: it reads the repository source, extracts every SQL
statement, and asserts that any statement touching a tenant-owned table
carries a tenant predicate — or is named here, with the reason it is safe.

It is deliberately a *contract* test rather than a live query test, so it
runs on every `cargo test` with no database at all. The live query half of
the same guarantee is `tests/live_pg.rs`, which runs against a real
PostgreSQL when `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set.

What it enforces:
1. every statement naming a tenant-owned table scopes by `tenant_id`,
unless it appears in [`ALLOWED_UNSCOPED`] with a written reason;
2. the durable schema carries the constraints the pipeline's correctness
depends on (tenant-scoped idempotency uniqueness, the one-open-attempt
fence, the claim index, outbox claim indexes, usage anti-double-metering);
3. no migration in the set is destructive.

It must NOT:
• become a place where violations are parked. Every entry in
[`ALLOWED_UNSCOPED`] states *why* the statement is safe, and the reason
must be a property of the statement (it runs under a tenant-scoped row
lock, it is keyed by an ownership fence, it is a global counter by
design), never "it is hard to fix";
• connect to a database. It is a source-level test.
```

```rust
// PURPOSE: The database-level half of the multi-tenant isolation guarantee:
// a static contract test over the SQL the durable pipeline actually issues.
//
// Owning layer: `mas-persistence` (the production repositories).
//
// Production responsibility: behavioural tests prove that tenant B is refused
// *today*. They cannot prove that the next statement someone adds is scoped.
// This file closes that gap: it reads the repository source, extracts every SQL
// statement, and asserts that any statement touching a tenant-owned table
// carries a tenant predicate — or is named here, with the reason it is safe.
//
// It is deliberately a *contract* test rather than a live query test, so it
// runs on every `cargo test` with no database at all. The live query half of
// the same guarantee is `tests/live_pg.rs`, which runs against a real
// PostgreSQL when `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set.
//
// What it enforces:
//   1. every statement naming a tenant-owned table scopes by `tenant_id`,
//      unless it appears in [`ALLOWED_UNSCOPED`] with a written reason;
//   2. the durable schema carries the constraints the pipeline's correctness
//      depends on (tenant-scoped idempotency uniqueness, the one-open-attempt
//      fence, the claim index, outbox claim indexes, usage anti-double-metering);
//   3. no migration in the set is destructive.
//
// It must NOT:
//   • become a place where violations are parked. Every entry in
//     [`ALLOWED_UNSCOPED`] states *why* the statement is safe, and the reason
//     must be a property of the statement (it runs under a tenant-scoped row
//     lock, it is keyed by an ownership fence, it is a global counter by
//     design), never "it is hard to fix";
//   • connect to a database. It is a source-level test.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What is tenant-owned
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Tables that hold one tenant's data and must never be read or written
/// without a tenant predicate.
const TENANT_OWNED_TABLES: [&str; 6] = [
    "executions",
    "tasks",
    "task_attempts",
    "outbox_events",
    "usage_records",
    "audit_events",
];

/// A statement that names a tenant-owned table without a tenant predicate,
/// together with the reason that is nevertheless correct.
///
/// Adding an entry here is a design decision and must be justified in the
/// `why` string. Three reasons recur, and they are the only ones in use:
///
/// * **row-locked** — the statement runs inside the same transaction as a
///   `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2` on the same row,
///   so the tenant was checked while the row was locked and cannot change
///   between the check and the write;
/// * **ownership-fenced** — the statement is keyed by `worker_id`/`locked_by`,
///   and holding the fence is itself proof of a prior tenant-scoped claim;
/// * **global-by-design** — a counter or gauge that is intentionally summed
///   across all tenants (backlog, capacity, claimable work).
struct Allowed {
    /// A distinctive substring identifying the statement.
    matches: &'static str,
    /// Why this statement is safe without a tenant predicate.
    why: &'static str,
}

const ALLOWED_UNSCOPED: [Allowed; 7] = [
    Allowed {
        matches: "FROM task_attempts WHERE id = $1",
        why: "row-locked: the attempt is loaded by id immediately after its \
              task was loaded with `WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2` in the \
              same transaction, so the tenant was already checked",
    },
    Allowed {
        matches: "UPDATE tasks SET version = $2",
        why: "row-locked: the settlement writes this row only after a \
              `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE ... WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2` \
              plus a version and ownership check inside the same transaction",
    },
    Allowed {
        matches: "UPDATE executions SET status = 'running'",
        why: "row-locked: the execution id came from the tenant-scoped claim \
              CTE that selected the task in the same transaction",
    },
    Allowed {
        matches: "UPDATE tasks SET locked_until = $3",
        why: "ownership-fenced: renewing a lease requires `locked_by` and \
              `status = 'running'`, which only a worker that already passed a \
              tenant-scoped claim can hold",
    },
    Allowed {
        matches: "UPDATE task_attempts SET lease_expires = $3",
        why: "ownership-fenced: keyed by (task_id, worker_id, status='running'), \
              the same fence the lease renewal holds",
    },
    Allowed {
        matches: "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task_attempts WHERE worker_id = $1",
        why: "global-by-design: active-attempt capacity is per worker, and a \
              worker is a deployment-level identity, not a tenant one",
    },
    Allowed {
        matches: "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM outbox_events WHERE status IN",
        why: "global-by-design: the outbox backlog is a relay health signal \
              summed across all tenants; the relay never reads payloads",
    },
];

/// Statements that intentionally span tenants because they are the *scheduler's*
/// view of all work, not one tenant's view.
const ALLOWED_GLOBAL: [&str; 1] = ["SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE status IN"];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Extracting the statements
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The repository root, resolved from this file's location.
fn workspace_file(relative: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    let candidate = root.join(relative);
    assert!(
        candidate.exists(),
        "expected {relative} to exist relative to {}",
        root.display()
    );
    candidate
}

/// Every string literal in a Rust source file.
///
/// `format!` bodies are plain literals before interpolation, so this captures
/// the SQL in both `sqlx::query("...")` and `sqlx::query(&format!("..."))`.
fn string_literals(source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let bytes = source.as_bytes();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        if bytes[i] == b'"' {
            let mut j = i + 1;
            let mut text = String::new();
            while j < bytes.len() {
                match bytes[j] {
                    b'\\' => {
                        if j + 1 < bytes.len() && bytes[j + 1] == b'"' {
                            text.push('"');
                        }
                        j += 2;
                    },
                    b'"' => break,
                    _ => {
                        // Source is ASCII SQL plus Rust; byte-wise slicing on a
                        // char boundary is safe for the files under test.
                        text.push(source[j..].chars().next().expect("char"));
                        j += 1;
                    },
                }
            }
            i = j + 1;
            out.push(text);
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// A SQL statement pulled out of the repository source.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Statement {
    /// Whitespace-collapsed SQL.
    sql: String,
    /// The tenant-owned tables it names.
    owned: Vec<&'static str>,
}

fn looks_like_sql(text: &str) -> bool {
    let upper = text.to_ascii_uppercase();
    ["SELECT", "INSERT INTO", "UPDATE", "DELETE FROM", "WITH "]
        .iter()
        .any(|keyword| upper.contains(keyword))
}

fn statements(source: &str) -> Vec<Statement> {
    string_literals(source)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|text| looks_like_sql(text))
        .map(|text| {
            let sql = text.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
            let mut owned = Vec::new();
            for table in TENANT_OWNED_TABLES {
                let pattern = format!("{table} ");
                if sql.contains(&pattern) || sql.ends_with(table) {
                    owned.push(table);
                }
            }
            Statement { sql, owned }
        })
        .filter(|statement| !statement.owned.is_empty())
        .collect()
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. Every tenant-owned statement is scoped — or is named, with a reason
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[test]
fn every_statement_naming_a_tenant_owned_table_is_tenant_scoped_or_allowlisted() {
    let source = std::fs::read_to_string(workspace_file("src/durable.rs"))
        .expect("read crates/persistence/src/durable.rs");

    let statements = statements(&source);
    assert!(
        statements.len() >= 20,
        "the extractor should find the durable pipeline's statements, found {}",
        statements.len()
    );

    for statement in &statements {
        if statement.sql.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("tenant_id") {
            continue;
        }
        let allowed = ALLOWED_UNSCOPED
            .iter()
            .any(|entry| statement.sql.contains(entry.matches))
            || ALLOWED_GLOBAL
                .iter()
                .any(|entry| statement.sql.contains(entry));
        assert!(
            allowed,
            "statement names tenant-owned table(s) {owned:?} with no tenant predicate and is \
             not allowlisted. Either scope it by tenant_id or add it to ALLOWED_UNSCOPED in \
             this file with a written reason.\n\n    {sql}",
            owned = statement.owned,
            sql = statement.sql
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn every_allowlist_entry_still_matches_a_real_statement() {
    // A stale entry is a silent hole: it would license a statement that no
    // longer exists while someone else's new unscoped statement gets waved
    // through by a rule nobody remembers writing.
    let source = std::fs::read_to_string(workspace_file("src/durable.rs"))
        .expect("read crates/persistence/src/durable.rs");
    let statements = statements(&source);

    for entry in &ALLOWED_UNSCOPED {
        assert!(
            statements
                .iter()
                .any(|statement| statement.sql.contains(entry.matches)),
            "allowlist entry {:?} no longer matches any statement; remove it",
            entry.matches
        );
        assert!(
            !entry.why.trim().is_empty(),
            "allowlist entry {:?} has no written reason",
            entry.matches
        );
    }
    for entry in ALLOWED_GLOBAL {
        assert!(
            statements
                .iter()
                .any(|statement| statement.sql.contains(entry)),
            "global allowlist entry {entry:?} no longer matches any statement; remove it"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_idempotency_lookup_is_tenant_scoped_and_uses_the_unique_index() {
    // The single most important tenant-scoped statement in the pipeline: the
    // DB-enforced idempotency lookup. If this were scoped by key alone, one
    // tenant could consume another tenant's key.
    let source = std::fs::read_to_string(workspace_file("src/durable.rs"))
        .expect("read crates/persistence/src/durable.rs");
    let idempotent: Vec<_> = statements(&source)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|statement| statement.sql.contains("idempotency_key = $2"))
        .collect();

    assert!(
        idempotent.len() >= 2,
        "both the execution and the task idempotency lookup must exist, found {}",
        idempotent.len()
    );
    for statement in &idempotent {
        assert!(
            statement.sql.contains("tenant_id = $1"),
            "an idempotency lookup must be scoped by tenant first: {}",
            statement.sql
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_claim_statement_scopes_by_tenant_before_it_locks_anything() {
    let source = std::fs::read_to_string(workspace_file("src/durable.rs"))
        .expect("read crates/persistence/src/durable.rs");
    let claim = statements(&source)
        .into_iter()
        .find(|statement| statement.sql.contains("FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED"))
        .expect("the durable claim statement must exist");

    assert!(
        claim.sql.contains("tenant_id = $2"),
        "a claim must be able to scope by tenant: {}",
        claim.sql
    );
    assert!(
        claim.sql.contains("FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED"),
        "the claim must skip locked rows so replicas never block each other"
    );
    assert!(
        claim.sql.contains("UPDATE tasks t SET"),
        "the fence must be installed by the same statement that selects the row: {}",
        claim.sql
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_settlement_loads_the_task_for_update_under_a_tenant_predicate() {
    // Without `FOR UPDATE` the version fence is a check-then-write race; two
    // settlements could both read version 3 and both write version 4.
    let source = std::fs::read_to_string(workspace_file("src/durable.rs"))
        .expect("read crates/persistence/src/durable.rs");
    assert!(
        statements(&source).iter().any(|statement| {
            statement
                .sql
                .contains("FROM tasks WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2")
                && statement.sql.contains("FOR UPDATE")
        }),
        "settlement must load the task FOR UPDATE under a tenant predicate"
    );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. The schema carries the constraints correctness depends on
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The durable pipeline migration.
fn migration_sql() -> String {
    std::fs::read_to_string(workspace_file(
        "../../migrations/0014_durable_pipeline/up.sql",
    ))
    .expect("read migrations/0014_durable_pipeline/up.sql")
}

#[test]
fn idempotency_is_unique_per_tenant_in_the_database() {
    // Spec: idempotency is enforced by the database, not by a
    // SELECT-then-INSERT. The unique index is the enforcement.
    let sql = migration_sql();
    assert!(
        sql.contains("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS executions_idempotency_idx")
            && sql.contains("ON executions (tenant_id, idempotency_key)"),
        "the idempotency key must be unique per tenant, enforced by the database"
    );
}

#[test]
fn duplicate_parallel_attempts_are_unrepresentable() {
    let sql = migration_sql();
    assert!(
        sql.contains("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS task_attempts_one_open_per_task")
            && sql.contains("ON task_attempts (task_id)")
            && sql.contains("WHERE status = 'running'"),
        "two workers must not be able to hold an open attempt on one task: the \
         database, not the application, is what makes that unrepresentable"
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_claim_hot_path_and_ownership_fences_are_indexed() {
    let sql = migration_sql();
    for (index, table) in [
        ("tasks_claim_idx", "tasks"),
        ("tasks_tenant_status_idx", "tasks"),
        ("tasks_owner_idx", "tasks"),
        ("tasks_lease_expiry_idx", "tasks"),
        ("outbox_events_claim_idx", "outbox_events"),
        ("outbox_events_stale_claim_idx", "outbox_events"),
        ("task_attempts_worker_active_idx", "task_attempts"),
    ] {
        assert!(
            sql.contains(&format!("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {index}"))
                || sql.contains(&format!("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {index}")),
            "missing {index} on {table}: the claim and lease-recovery paths must be indexed"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn usage_cannot_be_double_metered_for_one_task() {
    let sql = migration_sql();
    assert!(
        sql.contains("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS usage_records_task_dimension_idx"),
        "usage must be fenced against a duplicate write for the same task and dimension: \
         a retried settlement must never bill twice"
    );
}

#[test]
fn version_columns_exist_for_optimistic_concurrency() {
    let sql = migration_sql();
    assert!(
        sql.contains("ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS version             bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
        "executions and tasks need a version column for the optimistic fence"
    );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. No migration in the set is destructive
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[test]
fn no_migration_is_destructive() {
    let migrations_dir = workspace_file("../../migrations");
    let mut checked = 0;
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&migrations_dir).expect("read migrations") {
        let entry = entry.expect("entry");
        let up = entry.path().join("up.sql");
        if !up.exists() {
            continue;
        }
        let sql = std::fs::read_to_string(&up).expect("read up.sql");
        let upper = sql.to_ascii_uppercase();
        for forbidden in ["DROP TABLE", "DROP COLUMN", "TRUNCATE", "DELETE FROM"] {
            assert!(
                !upper.contains(forbidden),
                "{} contains `{forbidden}`: a production migration must be additive",
                up.display()
            );
        }
        checked += 1;
    }
    assert!(
        checked >= 14,
        "expected to check the whole migration set, checked {checked}"
    );
}
```

```text
The `mas-scheduler-service` crate manifest.
```

```toml
# PURPOSE: The `mas-scheduler-service` crate manifest.
#
# Owning layer: `mas-scheduler-service` (the process edge).
#
# Production responsibility: declare the scheduler process's dependencies,
# including `mas-application` for the canonical submission pipeline and
# `mas-events` for the outbox relay the process hosts.
#
# It must NOT:
#   • add the in-memory dev lane's dependencies to the default feature set;
#   • depend on `mas-api`;
#   • enable a feature that lets the process start without a durable store.

[package]
name = "mas-scheduler-service"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.85"
description = "Scheduler tick driver process: interval-driven runtime, dispatch adapters, in-flight ledger, completion listener"
license = "Proprietary"

[lib]
name = "mas_scheduler_service"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "mas-scheduler"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
mas-common = { workspace = true }
mas-domain = { workspace = true }
mas-scheduling = { workspace = true }
mas-worker = { workspace = true }
mas-application = { workspace = true }
mas-persistence = { workspace = true }
mas-contracts = { workspace = true }
mas-events = { workspace = true }
mas-messaging = { workspace = true }
sqlx = { workspace = true }
async-trait = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
uuid = { workspace = true }

axum = { workspace = true }
reqwest = { workspace = true }
serde = { workspace = true }
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["net", "signal", "rt-multi-thread"] }
tracing = { workspace = true }

[dev-dependencies]
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt", "time"] }
tower = { workspace = true }

[features]
# The outbox relay publishes over NATS, so the event plane is on by default.
# Building without it disables the relay rather than silently falling back to
# an in-process bus that would publish events nowhere.
default = ["nats"]
nats = ["mas-messaging/nats"]
testutils = []

[lints]
workspace = true

```

### FILE: `enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/scheduler-service/src/durable.rs`

**PURPOSE:**

_PURPOSE ব্লক এই ফাইলের হেডারে নেই; ফাইলটি জেনারেটেড বা কনফিগারেশন-মাত্র._

```rust
//! PURPOSE: The production scheduler dispatcher: due schedules become durable
//! executions and queued tasks through the real submission pipeline.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-scheduler-service`.
//!
//! Production responsibility: make a fired tick idempotent — the key is
//! derived from the schedule and the planned instant, so a replayed or
//! duplicated tick is answered by the pipeline's own idempotency rather than
//! creating a second run.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • submit outside the canonical pipeline;
//!   • create a task directly instead of through a submission;
//!   • treat "the tick fired" as "the work ran".

//! Production dispatcher: due runs become durable pending executions +
//! queued task rows through the *real* application submit pipeline.
//!
//! Design:
//! * Idempotency: `sched:<schedule_id>:<planned_unix_ms>`; a replayed tick
//!   returns `Started` of the SAME execution (the scheduler driver is
//!   at-least-once by design; the run journal stays singleton-true through
//!   the `schedule_runs` unique key + this key).
//! * Overlap bookkeeping rides `schedule_runs.detail`: `{"finished": true}`
//!   is stamped by [`DurableDispatcher::mark_finished`]; `is_running`
//!   reports dispatched-but-unfinished runs.
//! * Payload template contract (`schedules.target.task_template`):
//!   `{operation: "execution.run", input?: …, project_id: uuid,
//!    workflow_id?: uuid, agent_id?: uuid, priority?: …}` — any other
//!   operation class is a configuration bug and fails loudly per run.

use std::sync::Arc;

use mas_application::context::ServiceContext;
use mas_application::execution_service::ExecutionService;
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{AgentId, OrganizationId, ProjectId, ScheduleId, WorkflowId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_persistence::repositories::audit::PostgresAuditLog;
use mas_persistence::repositories::services::PgServices;
use mas_persistence::repositories::PgDurableExecution;
use mas_scheduling::due::DueWork;
use mas_scheduling::runner::{DispatchAck, DispatchPort};
use sqlx::PgPool;
use uuid::Uuid;

/// Dispatches due runs into the durable execution pipeline.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DurableDispatcher {
    pool: PgPool,
    replica_id: String,
}

impl DurableDispatcher {
    /// Binds a dispatcher to the shared pool + replica identity.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(pool: PgPool, replica_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            pool,
            replica_id: replica_id.into(),
        }
    }

    /// Org lookup for the run's scope (tenant FK holds the truth).
    async fn organization_of(&self, tenant: mas_common::ids::TenantId) -> Result<OrganizationId> {
        let org: Option<Uuid> =
            sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT organization_id FROM tenants WHERE id = $1")
                .bind(Uuid::from(tenant))
                .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
                .await
                .map_err(crate::squash_db)?;
        org.map(OrganizationId::from)
            .ok_or_else(|| AppError::validation("schedule dispatch: unknown tenant"))
    }

    /// Parses the schedule's materialization template.
    fn parse_template(template: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<ParsedTemplate> {
        let operation = template
            .get("operation")
            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or("");
        if operation != "execution.run" {
            return Err(AppError::validation(format!(
                "schedule template operation '{operation}' unsupported (expected execution.run)"
            )));
        }
        let uuid_field = |key: &str| -> Result<Option<Uuid>> {
            match template.get(key).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                None => Ok(None),
                Some(raw) => raw
                    .parse::<Uuid>()
                    .map(Some)
                    .map_err(|_| AppError::validation(format!("template {key} is not a uuid"))),
            }
        };
        Ok(ParsedTemplate {
            project: uuid_field("project_id")?,
            workflow: uuid_field("workflow_id")?,
            agent: uuid_field("agent_id")?,
            input: template
                .get("input")
                .cloned()
                .unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null),
        })
    }

    /// Idempotency key for one planned tick (stable across replicas).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn run_idempotency_key(work: &DueWork) -> String {
        format!(
            "sched:{}:{}",
            work.schedule_id.as_uuid(),
            work.planned_at.to_unix_ms()
        )
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
struct ParsedTemplate {
    project: Option<Uuid>,
    workflow: Option<Uuid>,
    agent: Option<Uuid>,
    input: serde_json::Value,
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl DispatchPort for DurableDispatcher {
    async fn dispatch(&self, work: &DueWork) -> Result<DispatchAck> {
        let parsed = Self::parse_template(&work.task_template)?;
        let Some(project) = parsed.project else {
            return Err(AppError::validation(
                "schedule template requires project_id (the run's scope)",
            ));
        };
        let organization = self.organization_of(work.tenant_id).await?;
        let ctx: ServiceContext =
            ServiceContext::for_service("mas-scheduler", &self.replica_id, &Timestamp::now())?
                .with_scope(work.tenant_id, organization);

        // Direct construction over THIS repo pool (service assembly is cheap;
        // each dispatch builds its own so transaction/context lifetimes stay
        // trivially correct).
        // Submissions from the scheduler land in the same durable pipeline the
        // API uses: one transaction, DB-enforced idempotency, real attempts.
        let execution_service = ExecutionService::new(
            Box::new(PgServices::new(self.pool.clone())),
            Box::new(PgServices::new(self.pool.clone())),
            Box::new(PgServices::new(self.pool.clone())),
            Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(self.pool.clone())),
            Arc::new(PgDurableExecution::new(self.pool.clone())),
        );
        let key = Self::run_idempotency_key(work);
        let outcome = execution_service
            .submit(
                &ctx,
                ProjectId::from(project),
                parsed.workflow.map(WorkflowId::from),
                parsed.agent.map(AgentId::from),
                parsed.input,
                Some(&key),
            )
            .await?;
        Ok(DispatchAck::Started {
            execution: outcome.execution.id,
        })
    }

    async fn is_running(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<bool> {
        let running: bool = sqlx::query_scalar(
            "SELECT EXISTS(
                SELECT 1 FROM schedule_runs
                WHERE schedule_id = $1
                  AND outcome = 'dispatched'
                  AND (detail ->> 'finished') IS NULL
            )",
        )
        .bind(Uuid::from(schedule))
        .fetch_one(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(crate::squash_db)?;
        Ok(running)
    }

    async fn mark_finished(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<()> {
        sqlx::query(
            "UPDATE schedule_runs
             SET detail = coalesce(detail, '{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('finished', true)
             WHERE schedule_id = $1
               AND outcome = 'dispatched'
               AND (detail ->> 'finished') IS NULL",
        )
        .bind(Uuid::from(schedule))
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(crate::squash_db)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample_work() -> DueWork {
        DueWork {
            schedule_id: ScheduleId::new(),
            tenant_id: mas_common::ids::TenantId::new(),
            planned_at: Timestamp::parse_rfc3339("2026-09-30T00:00:00.000Z").expect("ts"),
            task_template: serde_json::json!({"operation": "execution.run"}),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn idempotency_key_is_stable_and_distinguishing() {
        let work = sample_work();
        let key = DurableDispatcher::run_idempotency_key(&work);
        assert!(key.starts_with("sched:"));
        assert!(key.ends_with(":1790726400000"));
        let mut second = sample_work();
        second.planned_at = Timestamp::parse_rfc3339("2026-09-30T00:01:00.000Z").expect("ts");
        assert_ne!(DurableDispatcher::run_idempotency_key(&second), key);
    }

    #[test]
    fn template_parsing_rejects_non_execution_operations() {
        assert!(DurableDispatcher::parse_template(&serde_json::json!({
            "operation": "tool.invoke"
        }))
        .is_err());
        assert!(DurableDispatcher::parse_template(&serde_json::json!({
            "operation": "execution.run",
        }))
        .is_ok());
        let parsed = DurableDispatcher::parse_template(&serde_json::json!({
            "operation": "execution.run",
            "project_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000099",
            "input": {"beat": 1},
        }))
        .expect("parsed");
        assert_eq!(
            parsed.project.unwrap().to_string(),
            "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000099"
        );
    }
}
```

### FILE: `enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/scheduler-service/src/main.rs`

**PURPOSE:**

_PURPOSE ব্লক এই ফাইলের হেডারে নেই; ফাইলটি জেনারেটেড বা কনফিগারেশন-মাত্র._

```rust
//! PURPOSE: `mas-scheduler` process bootstrap: the schedule loop, the
//! outbox relay and graceful shutdown.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-scheduler-service` (the process edge).
//!
//! Production responsibility: bring up exactly one production path — due
//! schedules in, durable executions out, outbox events published — and refuse
//! to start when a production dependency (broker URL, database) is missing
//! rather than degrading into a silent no-op.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • run the in-memory dev lane without the explicit `--dev-inmemory` flag;
//!   • start the relay without a broker, or the loop without a durable store;
//!   • hold schedule state in process memory as if it were durable.

//! `mas-scheduler` process bootstrap.
//!
//! Bring-up modes:
//! * `--dev-inmemory` — in-memory schedule store + leases + loopback
//!   dispatcher + completion listener. Seeds one repeating schedule so the
//!   tick loop has visible work. Never production: no state survives.
//! * (default) — production composition: `mas_persistence::ScheduleStore`
//!   (due-scan + compare id) + `DurableDispatcher` (due runs become pending
//!   executions via the application pipeline) + `pg` schedule_runs journal
//!   as the cross-replica duplicate-fire guard.
//!
//! Environment (dev mode):
//! * `MAS_SCHEDULER_ADDR` — completion listener bind (default `127.0.0.1:8090`).
//! * `MAS_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MS` — tick interval (default `1000`).
//!
//! Production also runs the **transactional outbox relay** alongside the tick
//! driver: every event the platform writes inside a domain transaction is
//! claimed and published exactly once, with ownership fenced by a row lease so
//! several replicas may run it and a killed replica's rows come back.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use mas_common::ids::TenantId;
use mas_domain::{Schedule, ScheduleKind};
use mas_scheduler_service::dispatch::LoopbackDispatcher;
use mas_scheduler_service::driver::{DriverConfig, TickDriver};
use mas_scheduler_service::server::completion_router;
use mas_scheduling::lease::InMemoryLeaseStore;
use mas_scheduling::runner::{SchedulerConfig, SchedulerRuntime};
use mas_scheduling::store::InMemoryScheduleStore;
use mas_worker::grace;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    std::process::exit(match run().await {
        Ok(()) => 0,
        Err(err) => {
            eprintln!("mas-scheduler: {err}");
            2
        },
    });
}

async fn run() -> Result<(), String> {
    let dev_inmemory = std::env::args().skip(1).any(|arg| arg == "--dev-inmemory");
    if !dev_inmemory {
        return run_production().await;
    }

    // ── Ports ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    let store = InMemoryScheduleStore::new();
    let leases = InMemoryLeaseStore::new();

    // ── Seed: one heartbeat schedule, firing every 3 seconds ───────────
    let mut schedule = Schedule::new(
        TenantId::new(),
        None,
        "dev-heartbeat",
        ScheduleKind::Cron {
            expression: "*/2 * * * * *".to_owned(),
            timezone: "UTC".to_owned(),
        },
        serde_json::json!({"operation": "execution.run", "input": {"beat": true}}),
    )
    .map_err(|e| format!("seed schedule: {e}"))?;
    schedule.enable().map_err(|e| format!("enable: {e}"))?;
    store.seed(schedule.clone());

    // ── Layered configuration (files + env) ────────────────────────────
    let layered = mas_common::config::load_layered().map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let merger = mas_common::config::Merger::new(&layered);
    let addr = merger.string(
        "MAS_SCHEDULER_ADDR",
        "scheduler.completion_addr",
        "127.0.0.1:8090",
    );
    let replica_id = merger.string(
        "MAS_SCHEDULER_REPLICA_ID",
        "scheduler.replica_id",
        "scheduler-1",
    );
    let interval_ms = merger
        .u64(
            "MAS_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MS",
            "scheduler.tick_interval_ms",
            1_000,
        )
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let recover = merger
        .bool("MAS_SCHEDULER_RECOVER", "scheduler.recover_on_start", true)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let backoff_cap_ms = merger
        .u64(
            "MAS_SCHEDULER_BACKOFF_CAP_MS",
            "scheduler.error_backoff_cap_ms",
            30_000,
        )
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;

    // ── Dispatcher + completion listener ───────────────────────────────
    let dispatcher = LoopbackDispatcher::new();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(&addr)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("bind {addr}: {e}"))?;
    let app = completion_router(dispatcher.ledger().clone());
    let (handle, watch) = grace::channel();
    let mut http_watch = watch.clone();
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        axum::serve(listener, app)
            .with_graceful_shutdown(async move { http_watch.changed().await })
            .await
    });
    eprintln!("mas-scheduler dev: completion listener on {addr}");

    // ── Runtime + driver ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    let mut runtime = SchedulerRuntime::new(
        store,
        leases,
        dispatcher.clone(),
        SchedulerConfig::local(&replica_id).map_err(|e| format!("scheduler cfg: {e}"))?,
    )
    .map_err(|e| format!("runtime: {e}"))?;
    let mut driver = TickDriver::new(DriverConfig {
        tick_interval: std::time::Duration::from_millis(interval_ms),
        recover_on_start: recover,
        error_backoff_cap: std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_cap_ms),
    })
    .map_err(|e| format!("driver cfg: {e}"))?;

    tokio::spawn(grace::watch_signals(handle));
    eprintln!("mas-scheduler dev: ticking every {interval_ms}ms (ctrl-c to stop)");
    let stats = driver
        .run(&mut runtime, watch)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("driver: {e}"))?;
    eprintln!(
        "stopped: ticks={} dispatched={} errors={} lease_lost={} clean={}",
        stats.ticks,
        stats.dispatched,
        stats.consecutive_errors,
        stats.lease_lost,
        stats.stopped_by_shutdown,
    );
    Ok(())
}

/// Production path: durable store + durable dispatcher + journal-divided
/// fire protection (unique schedule_runs (schedule_id, planned_at)).
async fn run_production() -> Result<(), String> {
    use mas_persistence::pool::{Database, DatabaseUrl, PoolConfig};
    use mas_persistence::repositories::schedules::ScheduleStore;
    use mas_scheduler_service::durable::DurableDispatcher;

    let layered = mas_common::config::load_layered().map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let merger = mas_common::config::Merger::new(&layered);
    let replica_id = merger.string(
        "MAS_SCHEDULER_REPLICA_ID",
        "scheduler.replica_id",
        "scheduler-1",
    );
    let interval_ms = merger
        .u64(
            "MAS_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MS",
            "scheduler.tick_interval_ms",
            1_000,
        )
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let recover = merger
        .bool("MAS_SCHEDULER_RECOVER", "scheduler.recover_on_start", true)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let backoff_cap_ms = merger
        .u64(
            "MAS_SCHEDULER_BACKOFF_CAP_MS",
            "scheduler.error_backoff_cap_ms",
            30_000,
        )
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;

    // Outbox relay: the scheduler drains the transactional event outbox
    // alongside its tick driver, because it is already the process running a
    // durable loop against the same database with a graceful-drain path.
    let relay_enabled = merger
        .bool("MAS_OUTBOX_RELAY", "outbox.relay_enabled", true)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let relay_batch = merger
        .u64("MAS_OUTBOX_BATCH", "outbox.relay_batch", 64)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let relay_interval_ms = merger
        .u64("MAS_OUTBOX_INTERVAL_MS", "outbox.relay_interval_ms", 250)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let relay_lease_ms = merger
        .u64("MAS_OUTBOX_LEASE_MS", "outbox.relay_lease_ms", 30_000)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let nats_url = merger.string("MAS_NATS_URL", "broker.nats_url", "");

    let url = merger.string("MAS_DATABASE_URL", "database.url", "");
    if url.is_empty() {
        return Err("mas-scheduler production requires database.url / MAS_DATABASE_URL".to_owned());
    }
    let url = DatabaseUrl::new(url).map_err(|e| format!("database url: {e}"))?;
    let mut config =
        PoolConfig::for_url(url, "mas-scheduler").map_err(|e| format!("database config: {e}"))?;
    config.max_connections = 8;
    let database = Database::connect(&config)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("database: {e}"))?;
    let pool = database.pool().clone();

    // Migrations must be current: schedulers crash-loop promptly otherwise.
    let runner = mas_persistence::migrations::MigrationRunner::new(pool.clone());
    runner
        .ensure_table()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("migrations: {e}"))?;
    runner
        .verify()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("migration ledger drift — apply scripts/migrate.sh up first: {e}"))?;

    let store = ScheduleStore::new(pool.clone());
    let leases = InMemoryLeaseStore::new();
    let dispatcher = DurableDispatcher::new(pool.clone(), &replica_id);

    let mut runtime = SchedulerRuntime::new(
        store,
        leases,
        dispatcher,
        SchedulerConfig::local(&replica_id).map_err(|e| format!("scheduler cfg: {e}"))?,
    )
    .map_err(|e| format!("runtime: {e}"))?;
    let mut driver = TickDriver::new(DriverConfig {
        tick_interval: std::time::Duration::from_millis(interval_ms),
        recover_on_start: recover,
        error_backoff_cap: std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_cap_ms),
    })
    .map_err(|e| format!("driver cfg: {e}"))?;

    let (handle, watch) = grace::channel();
    tokio::spawn(mas_worker::grace::watch_signals(handle));
    eprintln!(
        "mas-scheduler production: replica={replica_id} tick={interval_ms}ms (journal-guarded fires)"
    );

    // ── Outbox relay ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Runs concurrently with the tick driver. Every event the platform writes
    // in a domain transaction lands here and is published exactly once; the
    // relay's only state is the row claim, so this replica can be killed at
    // any point and the rows come back.
    let relay = if relay_enabled {
        Some(
            spawn_outbox_relay(
                pool.clone(),
                &replica_id,
                &nats_url,
                relay_batch,
                Duration::from_millis(relay_interval_ms),
                Duration::from_millis(relay_lease_ms),
                watch.clone(),
            )
            .await?,
        )
    } else {
        eprintln!("mas-scheduler: outbox relay disabled by configuration");
        None
    };

    let stats = driver
        .run(&mut runtime, watch)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("driver: {e}"))?;
    eprintln!(
        "stopped: ticks={} dispatched={} errors={} clean={}",
        stats.ticks, stats.dispatched, stats.consecutive_errors, stats.stopped_by_shutdown,
    );

    if let Some(relay) = relay {
        relay.abort();
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Starts the outbox relay as a background task.
///
/// The relay drains the transactional outbox to the event bus. It owns no
/// state beyond the row claim, so it is safe to run several replicas and safe
/// to kill: rows whose claimant dies become claimable again after the lease.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns a boot failure when the bus cannot be reached. A relay that cannot
/// publish would claim rows and then fail every one of them, so refusing to
/// start is the useful behaviour.
async fn spawn_outbox_relay(
    pool: sqlx::PgPool,
    replica_id: &str,
    nats_url: &str,
    batch: u64,
    interval: Duration,
    lease: Duration,
    mut shutdown: mas_worker::grace::ShutdownWatch,
) -> Result<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>, String> {
    use mas_application::pipeline_metrics::PipelineMetrics;
    use mas_events::outbox::{OutboxRelay, OutboxStorePort, RetryPolicy};
    use mas_persistence::repositories::outbox::PostgresOutboxStore;

    if nats_url.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            "outbox relay requires broker.nats_url / MAS_NATS_URL: the event plane \
             is the only transport that publishes durable outbox rows, and \
             starting without it would dead-letter every event"
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "nats")]
    let bus: Arc<dyn mas_events::bus::EventBusPort> = Arc::new(
        mas_messaging::nats::NatsEventBus::connect(nats_url)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("outbox relay: event bus: {e}"))?,
    );

    // Built without the `nats` feature there is no production event transport,
    // and refusing to start is the only honest option: a bus that goes
    // nowhere would let the relay mark events published that nobody received.
    #[cfg(not(feature = "nats"))]
    let bus: Arc<dyn mas_events::bus::EventBusPort> = {
        let _ = nats_url;
        return Err(
            "outbox relay requires mas-scheduler built with the `nats` feature; \
             there is no in-process fallback for production event publication"
                .to_owned(),
        );
    };

    let store: Arc<dyn OutboxStorePort> = Arc::new(PostgresOutboxStore::new(pool));

    // The worker identity is unique per replica: two replicas sharing a claim
    // name could settle each other's rows.
    let worker = format!("{replica_id}-relay");
    let metrics = PipelineMetrics::default();
    let relay =
        OutboxRelay::new(store, bus, RetryPolicy::default(), worker.clone()).with_lease(lease);
    let batch = usize::try_from(batch.clamp(1, 1_000)).unwrap_or(64);

    eprintln!("mas-scheduler: outbox relay {worker} batch={batch} every {interval:?}");

    Ok(tokio::spawn(async move {
        loop {
            tokio::select! {
                _ = shutdown.changed() => {
                    eprintln!("mas-scheduler: outbox relay draining");
                    return;
                },
                _ = tokio::time::sleep(interval) => {},
            }

            match relay.relay_once(batch).await {
                Ok(cycle) if cycle.total() == 0 => {
                    // An empty cycle still says something worth recording: the
                    // backlog is drained. A gauge left at its last non-zero
                    // value would read as a permanent backlog.
                    metrics.set_outbox_backlog(0);
                },
                Ok(cycle) => {
                    // Emitted from the cycle the relay already reports, so the
                    // counters and the log line can never disagree.
                    metrics.set_outbox_backlog(i64::try_from(cycle.total()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX));
                    for _ in 0..cycle.dead_lettered {
                        metrics.dead_letter();
                    }
                    for _ in 0..cycle.lost {
                        metrics.stale_worker_rejection();
                    }
                    tracing::info!(
                        worker = %worker,
                        published = cycle.published,
                        dead_lettered = cycle.dead_lettered,
                        requeued = cycle.requeued,
                        released = cycle.released,
                        lost = cycle.lost,
                        "outbox relay cycle"
                    );
                },
                Err(error) => tracing::warn!(
                    worker = %worker,
                    %error,
                    "outbox relay cycle failed; the batch stays claimed until its lease expires"
                ),
            }
        }
    }))
}
```

**PURPOSE:**

```text
Declares the worker service binary and its dependencies.

Depends on `mas-ai-bridge` with default features only, which is what keeps
the in-memory bridge out of a release build, and on `mas-execution` for the
`AgentBridge` port the handler is written against.
```

```toml
# PURPOSE:
# Declares the worker service binary and its dependencies.
#
# Depends on `mas-ai-bridge` with default features only, which is what keeps
# the in-memory bridge out of a release build, and on `mas-execution` for the
# `AgentBridge` port the handler is written against.

[package]
name = "mas-worker-service"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT"
description = "Host binary for the mas-worker durable consumer (mirrors mas-scheduler-service)."

[[bin]]
name = "mas-worker"
path = "src/main.rs"
# The lib crate `mas-worker` owns the rustdoc output directory for this name;
# the binary is documented in the crate docs instead (avoids doc filename
# collision with the lib target).
doc = false

[dependencies]
mas-application = { workspace = true }
mas-common = { workspace = true }
mas-contracts = { workspace = true }
mas-domain = { workspace = true }
mas-messaging = { workspace = true }
mas-persistence = { workspace = true }
mas-worker = { workspace = true }
mas-scheduling = { workspace = true }
# The worker drives real AI execution. `mas-execution` is deliberately pulled in
# WITHOUT the `dev-bridges` feature: an in-memory agent bridge is never
# linkable into this binary, so production cannot select it by accident.
mas-execution = { workspace = true }
mas-orchestration = { workspace = true }
mas-ai-bridge = { workspace = true }
mas-security = { workspace = true }
sqlx = { workspace = true }
async-trait = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
tracing = { workspace = true }
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread", "signal"] }

[dev-dependencies]
toml = { workspace = true }

[features]
nats = ["mas-messaging/nats"]

```
